docs.title: The Runebase World Guide
docs.text:
Runebase World is the world of the Runebase games. Today you play it through the Runebase bot, in the Runebase Discord server and its partner servers (🌍 realms); the Runebase World web app, with its MMORPG, comes later, and many games will be playable in both. Each game's page says where you can play it. The games are all connected: what you catch, find and build in one game helps you in the others, and almost everything pays experience (your rank) and credits (the bot's money, which you can withdraw as Credits tokens on the Runebase blockchain).

Start here: chat in the server (your first message creates your account), then type /start. The main menu shows your rank card; Activities lists the games.

docs.title: What's in this guide
docs.text: Part What you'll find 🎫 Games every game, one by one: Hack & Slash, Crown of Chaos, heists, fishing, hunting, expeditions, cooking, the daily games, board games and prizes 🎒 Items and buffs every dish, ingredient, material, key, card and pet item: where you get it and what it does in each game; every buff by game 🎖️ Your account ranks, leaderboards and roles, credits and RUNES, buildings, pets, quests, the store, the basket, gifts, the convert market, the community rewards The MMORPG the open-world game of the Runebase World web app, coming later

docs.title: How the games connect
docs.text:
• Every day at 00:00 UTC your energy refills ( fishing, 🏹 hunting, 🧭 expeditions; heists: 3 energy, and you can be hit 6 times again), and the buildings' nightly production waits for you in Collect. Through the day: 15 🎰 Loot Reels spins, a 🔤 WordWeaver word every 4 hours, a single-player ♟️ chess game every 3 hours (5 paid wins a day) and 🏰 Hnefatafl (5 paid wins a day), the dice on a cooldown, a 🗣️ chat payout every 12 hours, the ⛰️ bump and 🗳️ vote windows. 🗝️ Piles and keys appear in the channels, and 🃏 Runes Pattern words keep coming.
  • Materials: fishing, hunting and expeditions fill your basket and pouch (fish, meat, scrap). The fire and the cooking table turn 🧺 fish, meat, spices and sauces into dishes: 🍲 buffs for the activities, the heists, Crown of Chaos and Hack & Slash. Scrap ( wood, metal, leather) from piles and activities pays for buildings, fire fuel and crafting; building supplies ( Toolbox, Nail, Rope) come from piles, prizes and the factories.
  • 🏗️ Buildings (each level needs a rank) give lasting bonuses: more energy, longer expeditions, better store prices, stronger heists and battles, and nightly production.
  • Credits come from the games' prizes, quests, piles, chests and WordWeaver, chess and Hnefatafl wins, and from the Iron Bank's interest. You spend them in the store, on gifts, scratch cards, Runes Pattern cards and clan registration. Credits come in from RUNES (or Credits token) deposits and Hermes purchases, and go out as Credits tokens through withdrawals; some prizes (dice, chests, scratch cards, Crown of Chaos) pay RUNES directly.
  • Experience comes from nearly everything and decides your 🥇 rank. Heists take experience from the defender and give experience to the attacker. Most games also have all-time and monthly 🏅 leaderboards with 🏷️ roles for the top players, and the heist and key hunt ladders can pay monthly RUNES prizes.
  • 🐾 Pets help in fishing, hunting, expeditions and heists while they're awake and cared for.

docs.title: What you can count on
docs.text:
• What a screen promises is what you're paid.
  • A double click, or two devices at once, never pays twice or spends twice.
  • If the bot restarts, nothing you earned is lost: trips, the nightly production and your games pick up where they were. While the bot is starting up, it answers "The bot is starting up…" and does nothing.
  • When something is refused (not enough energy, credits or items), you get a clear message and nothing is spent.
  • A refusal says why, where you clicked. A button on your own screen (a menu you opened) shows the reason on that screen, with a way back, as public or private as your screen is: a refused collect, craft, build, cook, store purchase or sale, chest key or scratch card from the menu, an expedition, fishing trip or hunt you can't start, a Crown skill that isn't ready, a refused bid, an auction listing, a heist or a clan action, a chess or Hnefatafl move. Only you see a refusal under a public post (a pile, a challenge, the Crown's post, a chest post, a ladder) or of a slash command: a button or menu that isn't yours, a command used too often, the dice on cooldown, /treasurechest without a key, a scratch card outside its channel, the bot starting up, an old button, /fish and /hunt without energy (with your fishing or hunting menu) or while you're busy, /fire without wood or in a channel where fires can't burn, a /gift you can't make (the receiver doesn't see it). What succeeds stays where it was: a trip, a fire, a gift and a store purchase still show in the channel.
  • Buttons on old messages from an earlier version of the bot only show a note.
  • Commands have a limit per 30 seconds. Past it the bot answers "Slow down!", only to you, every time, and does nothing. 2 uses: /info, /leaderboard, /poll, /price, /ranks, /withdraw; 5: /basket, /buildings, /convert, /craft, /equipment, /fire, /fish, /heist, /hunt, /loottables, /pouch, /quests, /rolepanel, /scratchcard, /settings, /start, /treasurechest, and /browseclans and /heistboard together; 10: /gift, /roll; 20: /hackslash; 30: /store. The buttons of the piles and keys allow 10 clicks in 20 seconds between them; past that, the same "Slow down!", only to you.

docs.title: 🎖️ Your account and the economy
docs.text:
What belongs to you across all the games, wherever you play them: your rank, your credits, your buildings and pets, your quests, and what you earn by taking part in the server.

Your account belongs to a 🌍 realm, the Discord server you play in: joining it, or your first chat message there, creates your account there (wallet, pouch, quests and daily energy), and every server you play in has its own.

Page What you'll find 🌍 Realms the Discord servers the bot plays in: one account in each, what each realm has of its own, what's only in the Runebase server 🥇 Ranks your rank, /ranks, the rank roles, losing experience 🏅 Leaderboards every leaderboard, all-time and monthly 🏷️ Roles top roles, the role panel Credits and RUNES deposits, withdrawals, buying credits with Hermes, RUNES prizes 🧱 Super stakers registering your Runebase super staker, its point every 8 hours, the super staker role Hodlers linking the address that holds your RUNES, the hodler roles by balance 🏗️ Buildings every building, its cost per level, what it does, nightly production, collecting, the Iron Bank 🐾 Pets tokens, care, day and night pets, every pet's perks, the kennel Quests what counts for each quest, Normal and Progressive quests, every quest's goal and rewards 🏪 Store the store's prices, buying and selling, the scrap discount 🧺 Basket what you gathered and cooked, kebabs eaten for experience 🎁 Gifts sending credits to another member ♻️ Convert Market swapping scrap and dishes at fixed rates 🗣️ Chat points what a message earns, the chat prizes, spam control ⛰️ Bumps bumping the server: experience, prizes, the bumper role 🗳️ Votes voting for the bot: experience, prizes, the voter role 🎨 Memes posting memes: experience, prizes, the memeologist role ✉️ Invites experience for the members you invite 👋 Joining and leaving the welcome, what leaving costs, coming back 🙋 Polls /poll: votes weighed by experience 🔍 Inspect looking at other players' Hack & Slash characters 📚 Info and the Hall of Honor the Info menu's pages: loot tables, consumables, the network, Stellar's xRUNES; the Hall of Honor

docs.title: 🧺 The basket
docs.text: /basket shows what you gathered and cooked. Swordfish Kebabs with Lemon and Rosemary can be eaten from the basket: each one gives 15 experience. More than you have, or an amount that isn't a whole number, eats nothing.

docs.title: 🏗️ Buildings
docs.text:
Buildings are yours alone: 3 resource buildings and 23 facilities you build and upgrade with building supplies and scrap. Most work on their own, wherever their effect applies (more energy, longer expeditions, better store prices, stronger heists and battles). Some produce something every night or let you make something every day, which you pick up in the Collect menu.

Where: /buildings to build and upgrade. /start → Activities → Collect for The Inn, Treasure Forge, Party Store, Nail Factory, Rope Factory and the Iron Bank.

docs.title: Every night: production
docs.text: At 00:00 UTC the resource buildings put their scrap in your pouch (up to its room), The Inn adds experience to its pool, and the Iron Bank adds interest to its pool. Each building produces once a day: if the bot restarts in the middle of the night's production, it finishes the day for exactly the buildings it hadn't reached, and pays nobody twice. If the bot is down at midnight, the day is produced once when it's back; a day the bot was down for entirely isn't made up. Resource buildings keep the fraction of a scrap they couldn't give (3.6 a day pays 3 and keeps 0.6 for the next night).

docs.title: Collecting
docs.text:
In Collect, each building shows what's waiting and what a collect costs. When the pool is empty, the day's collects are used up, or you're short of the scrap a collect costs, the button is off and nothing happens. A double click, or two devices, collect once: a click that comes too late collects nothing, and the collect screen says why ("there's nothing to collect", today's collects used, the scrap it costs).

  • The day's collects start again at 00:00 UTC: a collect at 23:59:59 UTC uses that day's, and at 00:00 UTC the next day's are there.
  • A Nail Factory or Rope Factory collect that completes a Collector quest shows the quest's rewards on the collect screen.
Key Metal Scrap each Bronze Key 1 Silver Key 2 Gold Key 3

Keys, Mystery Cards and scrap go into your pouch, which has room for this much per pouch level:

docs.title: The Iron Bank
docs.text:
The Iron Bank keeps credits for you and pays interest on them.

  1. Deposit credits, up to what your level can store.
  2. Every night it adds 0.25% of what's stored to its pool, up to the pool's size. Collect the pool for a few Metal Scrap.
  3. To take your credits out, Unbound them first. After the unbounding period you Withdraw them. Nothing is earned while they unbound.

Every credit the Iron Bank moves is in your wallet's history. A double click on Collect or Withdraw pays once, and a double click on Start Unbounding starts it once.

When the bank says no, its screen says why (as public or private as it is), and nothing moves: a deposit that isn't a positive amount (the smallest is 0.00000001 credits; typed as a plain number, rounded down to 8 decimals: 1.000000009 deposits 1, and 0x10 or 1e3 is refused), more than your wallet holds or more than the bank can still store; and anything an older screen still offers that no longer fits: a deposit while your credits unbound, unbounding when nothing is stored, a withdrawal before the unbounding period ends or when nothing unbounds. A second Withdraw (a double click, another device) is told there's nothing left to withdraw.

If something goes wrong while you deposit, start unbounding or withdraw, its screen says so ("Something went wrong, nothing was withdrawn."), nothing of it happened, and you can try again.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Upgrading needs both the resources and the rank: check the Preview for what each level gives and the whole road to the last level.
  • Collect The Inn and the Iron Bank before their pools fill up: a full pool earns nothing more.
  • Most buildings work without you doing anything; the energy buildings add their energy at the daily refill (00:00 UTC).

docs.title: ⛰️ Bumps
docs.text:
Bump the server with Disboard's /bump (or Discord Home's). The bumper gets 10 experience, a roll on the bump prize table and the bumper role for 2 hours, announced in the experience channel.

  • A server can be bumped once every 2 hours on each bump service (Disboard, Discord Home): a /bump answered in that window pays nobody, and the bot says the server was already bumped.
  • Two members' bumps answered at the same moment pay only one of them.
  • The bumper role is taken back when its 2 hours are over (also across a bot restart).

The prize table is without utilities (a 🪓 Wood Axe, 🔪 Skinning Knife or ⛏️ Mining Pick raises the scrap rows). A payout rolls its table once and pays at most one row, so the chances add up to at most 100%. The scrap rows come last: a utility makes them likelier and never takes anything from the other prizes (the Engraving Tool, the Chaos Relic, the pet tokens and the credits keep their chances at every utility level); past 100% the last scrap row, Wood Scrap, gives up what the other two gain. /loottables shows each prize's real chance for you. Every row of this table is played in the tests and pays exactly what it shows.

Prize Chance per bump 5 to 15 credits 8% 1 Nail 2% 1 Rope 0.4% 1 Common Pet Token 1% 1 📦 Pet Token (Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical) 0.5% each 1 Chaos Relic 5% 1 Engraving Tool 8% 1 Leather Scrap 24.35% 1 Metal Scrap 24.35% 1 Wood Scrap 24.35% nothing 0.05%

docs.text: • Bump when the 2-hour window is over: only the first bump in a window pays.

docs.title: 🗣️ Chat points
docs.text:
You earn experience and prizes just by talking in the server.

  • A message counts as a chat point when it has 5 or more words of at least 4 characters that weren't in your last counted message. Short or repeated messages earn nothing. The same message sent twice at once counts once.
  • Your 6th chat point within 12 hours pays 12 experience and a roll on the chat prize table, once, announced in the experience channel with your name. Later messages in those 12 hours only count chat points. When the 12 hours are over, a new round starts and pays again at its 6th point.
  • 40 chat points in the last 30 days make you an active chatter (a role); it goes again when old points drop out of the 30 days. A restart of the bot, even one in the middle of your message, never takes a chat point off early or counts it twice.
  • Chat points count on the chatter 🏅 leaderboards.

The prize table is without utilities (a 🪓 Wood Axe, 🔪 Skinning Knife or ⛏️ Mining Pick raises the scrap rows). A payout rolls its table once and pays at most one row, so the chances add up to at most 100%. The scrap rows come last: a utility makes them likelier and never takes anything from the other prizes ( Rope, Nail, the pet tokens and the credits keep their chances at every utility level). This table adds up to exactly 100%, so from the first utility level the last scrap row, Wood Scrap, gives up what the other two gain. /loottables shows each prize's real chance for you. Every row of this table is played in the tests and pays exactly what it shows.

Prize Chance per payout 1 to 8 credits 24.1% 1 Runes Pattern Card 5% 1 Chaos Relic 5% 1 Common Pet Token 1% 1 📦 Pet Token (Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical) 0.5% each 1 Nail 2% 1 Rope 0.4% 1 Leather Scrap 20% 1 Metal Scrap 20% 1 Wood Scrap 20%

docs.title: Spam control
docs.text: From your 5th message within a minute you get a warning; at the 8th you're timed out for a day. Admins are exempt.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Talk in full sentences: five real words of four letters or more make a chat point.

docs.title: Credits and RUNES
docs.text:
Credits are the bot's money. You earn them in the games, spend them in the store and elsewhere, and you can take them out of the game as Credits tokens on the Runebase blockchain, or bring RUNES in. Some prizes are paid in RUNES directly, from the realm's RUNES wallet.

Where: /pouch shows your balance, with Withdraw and Buy Credits. /withdraw withdraws directly.

/pouch shows the pouch's level, your credits, and the Bronze, Silver and Gold Keys, Mystery Cards and Wood, Leather and Metal Scrap it holds, each next to the room it has: per pouch level 40 Bronze, 20 Silver and 10 Gold Keys, 50 Mystery Cards and 100 of each scrap (level 2 holds twice that). Its buttons: Upgrade Pouch, Buy Credits, Withdraw, Withdrawal History and Credits Change History.

Upgrading the pouch: Upgrade Pouch shows the next level's room next to the current one, and its cost: 50 Leather Scrap times the pouch's level (50 for level 2, 100 for level 3, 150 for level 4, …), with how much of it you hold. Its own Upgrade Pouch button is off until you hold the cost, and the upgrade takes exactly that; Back to Pouch returns. The pouch is also in /start → Inventory → Pouch.

docs.title: Getting credits
docs.text:
• From the games: expeditions, piles, chests, chess and Hnefatafl wins, quests, WordWeaver, Loot Reels, dice, heists and more (each game's page has its prize table). A single credit prize above 25,000 credits is withheld instead of paid, and announced in the payout channel. The Crown of Chaos pool is the one exception: it's paid in full.
  • Gifts from other players (/gift, see 🎁 Gifts).
  • The Iron Bank pays interest on credits you store in it (🏗️ Buildings).
  • Deposits and buying credits with Hermes (below).

docs.title: Typing an amount
docs.text:
Wherever you type an amount of credits (a gift, an Iron Bank deposit, a withdrawal, buying credits with Hermes, an auction's prices and bids) it's read the same way:

  • A plain number: 5, 2.5, 0.00000001. Spaces around it don't matter.
  • 8 decimals at most, rounded down: 1.000000009 is 1 credit, never more than you typed.
  • Anything else is refused, and nothing moves (on the screen you typed it from; a withdrawal's answer only you see): 0x10, 1e3, +5, 1,5 (use a point), 1 000, Infinity.
  • Store quantities are whole numbers written the same way (5, not 5e0).

docs.title: Deposits
docs.text:
Pouch → Buy Credits shows your deposit address (it's made for you the first time; if the Runebase node is down, the menu says so and the address comes once it's back).

  • RUNES or Credits tokens sent to your deposit address become credits 1:1.
  • The bot sees the payment (you get a DM), then credits your wallet at 6 confirmations (another DM).
  • Each deposit is credited exactly once, however often the bot hears about it. A deposit made while the bot was offline is found and credited when it's back.
  • If the Runebase node or the bot's database has a hiccup while your deposit comes in, the bot tries again with the next block: a deposit is never skipped, and still credited only once.
  • One payment to several deposit addresses gives each player the sum sent to their own address.
  • A staking reward paid to a deposit address is not a deposit.
  • The deposit that verifies you as a 🧱 super staker goes to this same address and is credited like any other.

docs.title: Buying credits with Hermes
docs.text:
Pouch → Buy Credits → Buy Credits With Hermes, type the amount, Accept Purchase. Hermes charges your RUNES and the bot credits exactly the amount you asked for (1 RUNES = 1 credit), once. Fractions are fine (2.5 credits); an amount that isn't a plain number is refused, only you see it, and Hermes isn't asked.

  • If Hermes refuses, nothing is credited and you see why, in plain words.
  • The bot only credits an answer from Hermes that is about your purchase, for exactly that amount. If Hermes' answer gets lost, the screen says Hermes may have charged you and doesn't offer the purchase again (so you can't pay twice); the purchase isn't credited automatically, it's logged for the staff to sort out, so ask them. The same when Hermes' answer doesn't say what it charged, or your purchase was changed or settled by the staff while Hermes was answering: never credited twice.

docs.title: Withdrawals
docs.text:
/withdraw (address and amount), or Pouch → Withdraw. Only you see the result.

  • The address must be a Runebase address starting with R, and not your own deposit address.
  • At least 1 credit, at most your balance, typed as a plain number (2.000000009 withdraws 2). No fee: exactly the amount you withdraw is sent.
  • Your credits leave your wallet at once and the withdrawal is queued. The bot then sends it as Credits tokens and you get a DM ("Your withdrawal has been accepted", with the transaction), and another when it's confirmed at 6 confirmations. Your pouch history shows each withdrawal with its transaction.
  • If the Runebase node is down, /withdraw says so and nothing moves. If the node goes down after you queued, or the bot's wallet is short, the withdrawal stays queued and goes out later, once.
  • Withdrawals can be paused by the staff; a queued withdrawal then waits and goes out once they resume.
  • If the network refuses a withdrawal before it is sent, your credits are refunded, once, and you get a DM saying so.
  • A withdrawal is never sent twice. If the bot can't tell whether it went out (the node didn't answer clearly, or the bot stopped in the middle), it stays pending in your withdrawal history: the bot doesn't send it again or refund it on its own, and the staff check it and settle it.
  • Two withdrawals of your whole balance at the same moment: one is queued, the other is refused. Credits you spend after queuing can't touch the queued amount.

docs.title: RUNES prizes
docs.text:
Dice, treasure chests, scratch cards and Crown of Chaos pay some prizes in RUNES: a percentage of the realm's RUNES wallet, sent to you as a tip by the tipbot (Hermes). The prize tables show the percentages.

  • If the tipbot is offline, the dice roll, chest or scratch card says so, only to you, and nothing is spent; also when the bot can't read the realm's RUNES wallet (it lost the tipbot for over a minute). A Crown's reign still ends then, without RUNES.
  • The realm's RUNES wallet must hold more than 1 RUNES to pay RUNES prizes. With 1 RUNES or less every game still plays and pays everything else: the dice roll (experience, the prize draw, the cooldown), chests open, scratch cards are dealt and collected, a Crown's reign ends with its pool and experience. The prize tables show no RUNES, and a RUNES prize is shown as not paid: the realm's RUNES wallet is empty.
  • RUNES are paid only in a server whose tipbot is connected (today the Runebase server; the other servers are connected after the update). Until then a server plays like one with an empty wallet: the prize tables show no RUNES, a RUNES prize is shown as not paid: RUNES prizes aren't connected in this server yet, and everything else is paid.
  • No single RUNES prize is more than 1% of the realm's wallet. A prize above that would be a mistake in a prize table: the whole roll or card fails and nothing of it is paid (no experience, no item, no tip), and you can try again.
  • A tip is never sent twice. Each prize's tip is on record from the moment you win it. If the bot restarts right after your win, or the tipbot doesn't confirm the tip, the bot doesn't send it again on its own: the realm's admins are told, check the tipbot, and settle it by hand.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Double-check the withdrawal address: it must start with R.
  • Deposits take 6 confirmations; you get a DM when the bot first sees yours.

docs.title: 🎁 Gifts
docs.text:
/gift sends credits to another member. How credits get in and out of the game is in Credits and RUNES.

The receiver gets exactly what you send, it's recorded on both sides, and nothing is created or lost. A gift reaches a member who never used the bot too.

Nothing moves for an amount that isn't valid (a gift's amount is the rule for every amount you type: a plain number, rounded down to 8 decimals), a gift to yourself or to a bot, a member who can't be found, someone who isn't a member of this server ("… isn't a member of this server": a gift goes only to this server's members, to their account here), or more than you have, and only you see why (the receiver doesn't see it). A gift that goes through is shown in the channel as 🎁 Gift #N Success!. Two gifts at the same time can never spend the same credits twice.

docs.title: Hodlers
docs.text: Hold RUNES in your own wallet and show it: link one of your Runebase addresses, and the bot gives you the hodler role its balance reaches. Open it from /start → Ranks → Hodlers.

docs.title: The roles
docs.text: The Hodlers page lists the server's hodler roles, each with the RUNES balance it needs, the one you hold marked. Your linked address gets the highest role its balance reaches, and only that one: the bot checks every linked address again, one after another, for as long as it runs, so a balance that grows or shrinks moves your role up or down.

docs.title: Linking your address
docs.text:
1. The Hodlers page shows your own hodler deposit address (with its QR code) while no address is linked.
  2. Send any amount of RUNES to it from the address you want to link. The payment is what proves the address is yours; it isn't credited to your wallet (that's your /pouch deposit address, a different one).
  3. The address is linked: the page shows it, the bot tells you by DM, and you get the role its balance reaches.

docs.title: In more than one server
docs.text:
Each server has its own hodler roles, with its own balances; a server without any says "This server has no hodler roles yet." You can link the same address in every server you play in: each server shows its own hodler deposit address, and a payment to it links your address in that server only, so a wallet stays out of a server until you pay that server's address. One payment can pay several of your hodler deposit addresses at once and links each of them. Once linked, every server gives you its own role for the same balance.

An address belongs to one Discord account: if another player pays from an address you linked, they're refused, and their DM names the address.

docs.title: Unlinking
docs.text: Unlink Hodler Address asks first: Cancel keeps it, Confirm Unlink Hodler Address unlinks it and your hodler role goes. The page then shows your hodler deposit address again, to link another one.

docs.title: 📚 The Info menu and the Hall of Honor
docs.text:
/start → Info has the bot's reference pages. Each page replaces the menu (privately if you play privately) and has Main Menu and a way back to the Info menu.

  • Game Guide: this guide. Airdrop Schedule: the server's airdrops, on Hermes.
  • About RuneBase: what Runebase is, its wallets, explorers and exchanges.
  • Network Info: the Runebase network as the bot's node sees it: the block height, the block reward, the network's difficulty and weight, the coins in circulation and the estimated yearly staking return, with links to the website and the explorer, and the 🧱 super stakers.
  • Loot Tables: the prize table of each activity, with each prize's real chance for you (your utilities can push the last prizes out). Chess has one table per difficulty (Easy, Medium, Hard); a long table, like Loot Reels', comes in pages of 35 with Next and Previous.
  • Consumables: one page per consumable, picked in its menu: what it does, and how many you hold.
  • Treasure Hunting: how keys spawn and what the treasure hunter role gives (🗝️ Piles and the key hunt), with your own role's time left.
  • Talkative: how 🗣️ chat points work, with your points this round, this month and all time.
  • Memeologist: how 🎨 meme points work, with your cooldown and your points.
  • Stellar (xRUNES): xRUNES LP lists the xRUNES liquidity pools on Stellar; xRUNES Daily Trade Contest ranks the day's xRUNES buyers, 10 a page: Previous Day goes back a day at a time, Next Day comes back up to today.

docs.title: The Hall of Honor
docs.text: /start → Hall of Honor thanks the people and tools behind the bot's art and code; Donations shows how to support its development, and Back to Hall of Honor returns.

docs.title: 🔍 Inspect
docs.text: /start → Activities → Inspect lets you look at other players' Hack & Slash characters, if they allow it. Nothing is open by default: turn on Hack & Slash Inspection under Inspect → Inspect Settings to let others see your characters, their stats, skills and equipment. The equipment view lists every slot (Helm, Amulet, Main Hand, Off Hand, Armor, Gloves, both rings, Belt, Boots…) with the item worn there or "Empty Slot", under a picture of the character's gear.

docs.title: What others can see
docs.text: Each part of your account has its own switch under Inspect Settings: Pouch, Basket, Buildings, Hack & Slash, Utilities, Fishing Gear, Hunting Gear and Crown of Chaos. When you pick someone in Select a user!, the screen lists what they allow, with an Inspect button for each: their pouch (credits, keys, cards and scrap), their basket, their buildings, utilities, fishing and hunting gear, and their Crown of Chaos points. Back to Inspect returns to them.

docs.title: Your whitelist
docs.text: With whitelist mode on (Settings → Inspect Whitelist), only the members on your whitelist can inspect you; everyone else is told they're not on it and sees no Inspect buttons. Inspect → Manage Whitelist adds and removes members (up to 200) and shows whether whitelist mode is on.

docs.title: ✉️ Invites
docs.text: When someone joins the Runebase server through your invite (invites count only there, see 🌍 Realms), you earn 25 experience once they reach 100 🗣️ chat points. Once per invited member; the reward is posted as ✉️ Invite Reward.

docs.title: 👋 Joining and leaving the server
docs.text: What happens when you join the server and when you leave it.

docs.title: Joining
docs.text: A new member of the home server gets the inactive-chatter role and is welcomed in the welcome channel once verified; others can wave at them. The welcome post's Open RuneBase World Menu opens the main menu for whoever presses it, their own (privately for a player who plays privately); the post stays as it is.

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text: Leaving the server costs 250 experience (never below 0) in that server only (your accounts in other 🌍 realms are untouched), announced in the server's experience channel (a server without one takes the experience all the same, unannounced), and takes you off every 🏅 leaderboard and its 🏷️ roles right away. Coming back puts you back in the server's lists: your 🥇 rank role, your scores on the boards and the top roles you rank for.

docs.title: 🏅 Leaderboards
docs.text:
Most games have leaderboards, all-time and monthly, whose top players hold a role.

/leaderboard (or /start → Ranks → Leaderboards) opens the experience leaderboard, with two menus to pick an all-time or a monthly board.

  • A board shows 10 players a page; a longer one has Next and Previous, a shorter one a Close button. The key hunt ladder also has Previous Month and, on an earlier month, Next Month.

  • Boards show the top players in score order; on a tie, the newer Discord account comes first (the key hunt ladder puts whoever got there first). Only players with points are listed, and only players who are in the server.

  • Monthly boards count the last 30 days: every point you earn leaves the monthly board about 30 days later. (The key hunt ladder counts the calendar month, and so does the heist ladder on /heistboard.) A restart of the bot, even one in the middle of your action, never takes a point off a monthly board early or counts it twice.
  • The Monthly Accelerator board counts your experience gains of the last 30 days, minus what you lost.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Monthly boards forget points after 30 days: keep playing to keep your place.

docs.title: 🎨 Memes
docs.text:
A meme posted in a meme channel pays 8 experience and a roll on the meme prize table, once per cooldown.

  • Deleting one of your memes while your latest meme is under 4 hours old takes 10 experience back. Deleting a meme within a week of posting takes its point off the monthly meme board.
  • Your 25th meme in the last 30 days makes you a memeologist (a role).

The prize table is without utilities (a 🪓 Wood Axe, 🔪 Skinning Knife or ⛏️ Mining Pick raises the scrap rows; they come last, so a utility never takes anything from the other prizes). Every row of this table is played in the tests and pays exactly what it shows.

Prize Chance per meme 1 to 7 credits 7% 1 Runes Pattern Card 5% 1 Chaos Relic 5% 1 Nail 2% 1 Rope 0.4% 1 Engraving Tool 5% 1 Common Pet Token 1% 1 📦 Pet Token (Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical) 0.5% each 1 Leather Scrap 20% 1 Metal Scrap 20% 1 Wood Scrap 20% nothing 12.1%

docs.title: 🐾 Pets
docs.text:
Pets come from pet tokens. Your active pet helps you in fishing, hunting, expeditions, heists and Crown of Chaos while it's awake and well cared for, and it earns pet points for the pet leaderboards. It needs food, washing, play and sometimes a cure, and its stats change every minute, also while you're away.

Where: /start → Activities → Pet.

docs.title: Getting a pet
docs.text:
Consume a pet token from the pet menu. Each Consume spends exactly one token and gives at most one pet: the token has a chance to find a pet of its rarity, picked from that rarity's pets. If it finds a pet you already have, the token is used up and you get nothing. Your first pet becomes your active pet. Without a token, nothing happens.

Tokens also drop from many activities (fishing, hunting, expeditions, heists, chat, bumps, votes, dice, Loot Reels…): see each game's prize table.

docs.title: Caring for your pet
docs.text:
Action Costs Notes Feed one Pet Food of the pet's rarity Wash one Pet Wash Kit of the pet's rarity Cure one Pet Cure of the pet's rarity Play nothing

Each action moves the pet's stats (hunger, energy, happiness, hygiene, sickness) by that pet's own table, and gives the pet 1 experience, unless the action hits a bad condition (playing with a dirty pet, for example): then no experience. Pet items are sold in the pet menu and the store:

docs.title: Awake and asleep
docs.text: Each pet is a day pet or a night pet. A day pet is awake with the lights on, a night pet with the lights off; the light switch in the pet menu changes it. An asleep pet can't be played with or fed (nothing is spent), and its perks don't work.

docs.title: Every minute
docs.text:
While you're away, your active pet's stats move every minute by its awake or asleep table. Stats always stay between 0 and 100.

A pet left alone for 30 days stops changing (no stat changes, no points, no perks). Play with it or use the light switch, and it carries on from the stats it had.

docs.title: Pet points
docs.text:
Your active pet earns pet points every minute, awake or asleep, from its stats after the minute's change: the better fed (low hunger), happier, cleaner and healthier it is, the more (energy counts a little). A rarer pet earns more for the same stats: ×1.05 Uncommon, ×1.1 Rare, ×1.15 Epic, ×1.2 Legendary, ×1.25 Mythical. A pet in a bad state earns nothing. The pet menu shows it as Score per Minute.

  • Only the minute earns points: feeding, washing, curing and playing give your pet experience, not points; a pet resting in the Pet Kennel earns nothing; activities, heists and the Crown give no pet points.
  • The points wait, and go onto the All-Time Pet Points and Monthly Pet Points 🏅 leaderboards every 15 minutes, also when your pet has fallen into a bad state since (before the update, points earned before a pet fell ill could stay waiting and be lost). Changing pets or putting your pet in the kennel puts its waiting points on the boards first, for that pet. Two clicks at once never count them twice, and a restart of the bot keeps them waiting.
  • The monthly board counts the last 30 days: each batch of points leaves it (and your pet's monthly score) about 30 days later; the all-time board keeps them. The top 10 of each board hold its role.

docs.title: Perks
docs.text:
Every pet has perks for the activities. A perk works only while the pet is awake and its stats meet the perk's conditions. Only your active pet counts: a pet in the kennel or among your favorites adds nothing. Every perk below is checked in play at exactly its number, on its game's screen and in the game itself, awake and asleep. A fishing, hunting or expedition trip uses the pet that is active and awake when the trip ends: change pets during a trip and the new pet's perks count; put it to sleep and none do. A fishing or hunting perk adds its points to the chance of one fish or animal, and only helps if your rod or rifle catches it. An expedition perk adds its points to one expedition's scrap. A Crown of Chaos perk helps either your attacks on the Crown ("attacking the Crown") or you while you hold the Crown ("holding the Crown"): a Dog's extra 1-2 damage counts on every attack while it's awake, and stops when you turn its lights off.

docs.title: Changing pets, favorites, nicknames
docs.text:
• Change Pet makes another of your pets the active one. The old pet keeps its stats and the points it earned. The Pet Perks screen there shows each perk as it works: an extra damage range as "+1-2".
  • Favorites: 5 slots for quick switching from a menu. A sixth is refused.
  • Nickname: 2 to 50 characters; spaces at the ends are trimmed, and mentions and formatting are removed.

docs.title: The kennel
docs.text: The Pet Kennel building holds as many pets as its level (🏗️ Buildings). Only a pet in good condition can go in (the menu tells you what to improve first). In the kennel a pet rests and regains energy every minute; at full energy it leaves the kennel, and you can ask for a DM when that happens.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Check whether your pet is a day or a night pet: its perks only work while it's awake.
  • Match your pet to your gear: a fishing perk for a fish your rod doesn't catch does nothing.
  • Keep the stats up (happiness, energy, low sickness): below a perk's conditions it stops working.

docs.title: 🙋 Polls
docs.text: /poll posts a poll (🙋 Poll #N) with a button per answer. Your vote weighs your experience ÷ 350 (rounded down); under 350 experience you can't vote. You vote once. When the time is up, the result shows every answer's weight and voters, and the winner. A poll running when the bot restarts keeps going.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
Quests are long-running goals behind almost everything you do: a vote, a fishing trip, a cooked dish, a chess win, a heist all count toward a quest. When a quest reaches its goal it completes on its own, pays its experience and rewards, and starts its next level.

Where: /quests opens your quest log. Pick Normal or Progressive, then a quest: it shows what counts, your progress toward the goal, and the rewards of its next completion with their chances.

docs.title: Two kinds of every quest
docs.text:
Every quest exists twice, and what you do counts toward both:

  • Normal Repeatable: the same goal and the same rewards at every level. Some rewards are certain, others have a chance (the tables below).
  • Progressive Repeatable: every level asks more and pays more. The goal grows by 60% of the first level's goal a level and the experience and rewards by 40% (Runes Pattern and the Crown of Chaos quests: 50% and 30%). Every reward is certain. Level 10 of Vote asks 128 votes.

docs.title: Completing a quest
docs.text:
• When your progress reaches the goal, the quest completes by itself: its experience and rewards are paid once, the quest goes up a level, and the progress beyond the goal is kept for the next level.
  • Quests never reset. A quest keeps its level and progress until you complete it: no new day, week or month starts it over.
  • One action can complete many levels: a cooking batch of 1,500 dishes completed 52 levels, each paid as its level says. A quest completes at most 100 levels in one action (normal and progressive alike); the rest stays as progress, and your next action that counts toward it goes on (601 Cooking levels waiting complete 100 a cook).
  • A quest's experience comes on top of the action's own (a chess win that completes Chess - Win (Easy) pays the win's 15 and the quest's 50).
  • No single action pays more than 15,000 experience, quests included, in every game alike; within it, a quest's experience is paid in full, never cut (a chess win, a Loot Reels spin and the Crown of Chaos used to cut an action at about 9,000). Nothing in the game comes close (a batch of 5,000 dishes pays about 9,300 with its quests), and 100 levels of a normal quest stay below it. An action that would still pass it is stopped whole: nothing is spent or paid, your quest progress stays, and the cooking table tells you.
  • The action's result lists what its quests paid, in one message. Each quest shows once, with its levels together: "Quest Complete: Cooking #1-#20" (20 levels), their experience and rewards added up. At most 4 quests get a box of their own; with more, 3 do and the last box lists the others.
  • The Nail Factory and the Rope Factory show the quests a collect completes on the collect screen. The nightly production (your resource buildings' scrap, counted toward Scrapper) completes its levels without a message: you find them paid in /quests and in your pouch.
  • One action can complete several quests, and each pays once: a fishing trip completes Fishing and each fish's quest, a heist completes quests for both players, the Crown of Chaos round for the Crown and every player whose bleed or doomseed hit. Their experience is added up with the action's own and paid once.
  • A heist's public log lists both players' quests in their loot summaries, with a box of their own for those that fit in the message.
  • A reward your pouch has no room for (keys, scrap, Mystery Cards) is not received, and the result says so. When many levels complete at once and the pouch fills partway, the rewards that fit are received and the rest aren't: 15 levels of Reel of Fortune with room for 2 Gold Keys pay 2 and show the other 13 as not received; their credits are paid in full.
  • Two actions at the same moment one short of the goal complete the quest once, and everything both did counts (a supply pile and the Nail Factory collected together, two cooks at two fires).
  • A restart in the middle of a trip's completion loses nothing: the trip completes at the next start, and its quests count and pay once.
  • The Hnefatafl quests pay their rewards but no experience.
  • Every player has every quest: players who joined before a quest existed get it at level 1 with this release, and keep the quests they had.

docs.title: What counts
docs.text:
Each quest's own text says what counts (the tables below). In short:

You Counts toward go fishing or 🏹 hunting Fishing / Hunting: the trip's energy; the quest of each fish or animal: what you catch go on an 🧭 expedition Expeditions and that expedition's quest: the expedition's seconds cook Cooking and the recipe's quest: every dish, Cuisine Cottage extras included 🗳️ vote, ⛰️ bump Vote, Bump: each rewarded one win a ⚔️ quick battle QuickBattle: 1, once roll the dice Dice: each paid roll spin 🎰 Loot Reels Reel of Fortune: each spin solve a 🔤 WordWeaver word WordWeaver - Solved win a ♟️ chess or 🏰 Hnefatafl game against the bot the Win quest of that difficulty: each paid win win 🃏 Runes Pattern Runes Pattern - Win collect a key pile the Treasure Hunt quest of that key collect a scrap pile the Scrapper quest of that scrap; your resource building's nightly scrap counts too collect a supply pile Collector - Nail / Rope: the Nails or Ropes you got; the Nail Factory and the Rope Factory count what they make (28 nails, 7 ropes) 🤺 attack the Crown of Chaos Damage Dealt: your attack's damage, and your bleeds' and seeds' damage in the rounds 👑 hold the Crown Points Earned: each point the Crown earns in a round 🗡️ heist Experience Stolen (what you gained), Experience Lost (what the heist took: its full amount, even when you had less), Block, Recover (the attacker's energy kept: a defender never gets energy back from a counter-attack, so only your own attacks count), Counter-Attack

What is refused counts nothing: a trip or a cook that doesn't start, a roll on cooldown or with the tipbot offline, the 16th spin of the day, a wrong guess, a lost game, a 6th chess or Hnefatafl win of the day, a vote within its 12 hours, a bump while the server is still bumped, a factory collect over the day's limit, a missed attack on the Crown. Credit piles and treasure chests count toward no quest.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Quests never get in the way: just play, and check /quests to see what's close to completing.
  • Big actions (a long expedition, a large cooking batch) can complete several levels at once.
  • Keep room in your pouch: a key or a Mystery Card from a quest is lost when the pouch is full.

docs.title: 🥇 Ranks
docs.text:
Nearly everything you do pays experience. Experience gives you a rank in the realm, and ranks unlock building levels and more.

  • Your rank is the highest rank of the realm whose experience you have reached (each server sets its own ranks). One big gain across several ranks takes you straight to the highest, with one announcement.
  • /ranks (or /start → Ranks → Ranks) shows your rank, your experience and how much is left to the next rank, on the page of the realm's ranks that holds yours: 10 ranks a page, with Previous and Next through all of them.
  • Your rank comes with the rank's role; the role of your old rank goes. Rank changes are announced once, in the ranks channel: Level Up! ("You leveled up to …") or Level Down! ("You lost a level! You are now …").
  • You can lose experience (heists, leaving the server, a deleted 🎨 meme). Below the first rank's experience you are Unranked, without a rank role.
  • Ranks unlock building levels (🏗️ Buildings).

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • /ranks tells you how far the next rank is.

docs.title: 🌍 Realms
docs.text: A realm is a Discord server the Runebase bot plays in. The Runebase Discord server is the home realm, and every partner server that added the bot is a realm too. Everything in this guide happens inside one realm: the server you're in when you type a command or press a button.

docs.title: One account in each realm
docs.text:
Joining a realm's server, or your first message there, opens your account in that realm: a credits wallet, a pouch, quests and daily energy. Play in two servers and you have two accounts, each with its own:

  • experience and 🥇 rank: each server has its own ranks, and the rank roles you get are that server's;
  • credits: each realm's wallet has its own deposit address (Pouch → Buy Credits shows the one of the realm you're in, and RUNES or Credits sent to it land in that realm's wallet only; Recent Deposits lists that address's deposits); withdrawals and credits bought with Hermes go from and to the wallet of the realm you're in; a 🎁 gift is paid from your account in the realm you send it in, to the receiver's account in that realm, and only to a member of that server (anyone else is refused, and nothing moves);
  • pouch (keys, scrap, Mystery Cards), 🧺 basket, 🏗️ buildings, 🐾 pets, quests and daily energy;
  • 👹 Hack & Slash character, with its items, stash and 🔨 auction house listings: a Warrior in one server, you pick a class again in the other;
  • heist role and clan: joining the heist in one server doesn't put you in another's, and each server's role panel sets the experience it asks, counted in that server;
  • dice cooldown: a roll in one server doesn't stop you rolling in another;
  • places on the 🏅 leaderboards, the monthly boards and the ladders, and the 🏷️ roles they give;
  • /settings.

What you earn in one realm leaves your account in the other as it was: nothing moves from one realm to another by itself. Leaving a realm's server costs 250 experience there and takes you off its boards, and only there; your account stays and is yours again when you come back (👋 Joining and leaving).

docs.title: What every realm has of its own
docs.text:
• Its own Crown of Chaos: one Crown, its pool and its weekly ladder.
  • Its own 🗿 Jotnar giants, posted in its Hack & Slash channel and fought by that server's players.
  • Its own 🏪 store, with its own stock: what you pay goes to that realm's store, and the 5% on top to that realm's Crown pool.
  • Every kind of pile (🗝️ Piles): treasure keys, scrap, Rope, Nail and credit piles, on the same schedule in every realm, in channels its verified members can see. What you collect goes to your account there, with that realm's key hunt, 4-hour key windows and treasure hunter role.
  • Treasure chests and scratch cards, opened and dealt with the keys and Mystery Cards of that realm's pouch, in its own chest and scratch card channels (a realm whose admins haven't set them opens and deals none).
  • Its own RUNES wallet, kept by the tipbot (Hermes): a RUNES prize ( dice, chests, scratch cards, the Crown's reward) is a share of the wallet of the realm you play in, so a realm whose wallet is empty (1 RUNES or less) pays no RUNES: everything else of those games is paid as usual. RUNES are paid only where the realm's tipbot is connected: today the Runebase server; the other realms are connected after the update, and until then they pay no RUNES the same way (the screens say "RUNES prizes aren't connected in this server yet").
  • Its own hodler roles, with its own balances; the same linked address can hold a role in every server you play in.
  • Its own channels and roles for each game, set by its admins: a dice roll outside the dice channel is posted in that realm's dice channel, rank changes in its ranks channel.
  • Its own welcome: a realm whose admins set a welcome channel welcomes its newly verified members there, by the server's own name.
  • Its own admins: a server's admins (Discord's Administrator permission) set its roles and channels with /config; that's all an admin of a server can do with the bot. Spawning piles and the maintenance and test commands belong to the bot's own operator.

A server that adds the bot or is switched on as a realm plays at once: its commands appear, and chatting and joining count from then on.

docs.title: Partner roles
docs.text: A member of both the Runebase server and a partner server gets the partner's role in the Runebase server, and the Runebase server's role in the partner server where one is set up, each announced in that server's experience channel. Leaving the partner server takes them back.

docs.title: Only in the Runebase server
docs.text:
• ✉️ Invite rewards are counted only there: joining a partner server through an invite counts for nobody.
  • New members get the inactive-chatter role there only, and only its staff see who joined.

docs.title: 🏷️ Roles
docs.text: The top players of many 🏅 leaderboards hold a role, and /rolepanel has roles you can give yourself.

docs.title: Top roles
docs.text:
Many boards give a role to their top 10 players (the experience board also to the top 20 and top 30). When you pass someone, the role moves to you; when you drop out, it goes to the next player.

  • A board with fewer than 10 players who scored gives its role only to those who scored.
  • After a restart, the roles match /leaderboard again.
  • Leaving the server takes you off the boards at once, and your top roles go to the next players. Points you'd lose while away don't put you back; coming back does.

docs.title: The role panel
docs.text: /rolepanel shows the roles you can give yourself, one at a time (pick one in Select Role). Press Earn to take it or Remove to give it back. Some roles need a minimum amount of experience: below it, the panel shows the role with the button off. Only the player who opened the panel can use its buttons.

docs.title: 🏪 The store
docs.text:
The store sells you items for credits and buys them back. How credits get in and out of the game is in Credits and RUNES.

Where: /store. Pick a category and an item, then Buy or Sell and type how many. Some other menus open the store on an item (the 🤺 Crown of Chaos menu's Buy Chaos Relic), and the store's delivery announcements have Buy … buttons for what just arrived.

What the screen shows: your credits, how many of the item you have, the price to Buy one and what Sell pays for one (with its percent), the store's own balance and the Crown of Chaos pool.

  • The price on the screen is what you pay, to the last fraction of a credit: one costs exactly the price shown, several of a fixed-price item exactly the price × the amount (crafting materials: below), and you get exactly the amount. On top of that the game adds 5% of what you pay to the Crown of Chaos pool; you don't pay it.
  • Selling pays exactly the amount the screen shows × how many you sell, and takes exactly that many. Most items sell back for 75% of their price (the Forgotten Throne Elixir for 2.5%). The Trade Post building adds 0.15% of the price per level (75% becomes 90% at level 100; the elixir's 2.5% becomes 17.5%), and the screen shows it.
  • The store pays from its own balance, which grows with every purchase in your server. When it doesn't have enough for your sale, the sale is refused and you keep your items. The Party Store building gives no store discount.
  • Every purchase and sale is one line in your credits history, and one in the store's Purchase History button: newest first, 25 a page, with how many, the total and the price of one.
  • When the store says no, the store screen says why (as public or private as it is), and nothing changes: an amount that isn't a whole number above 0 written plainly (5; 1e3, 0x10, +5 and 1,000 aren't amounts), more than your wallet holds, selling more than you have, more than the store has in stock, a full pouch.
  • At the same moment: a double click, two devices, or two players after the last one never pay twice, sell twice or get more than the store has: one goes through, the other is told why. A buy or sell box you closed never takes over your next purchase.
  • Scrap: every day (from 00:00 UTC) your first 5 scrap cost a quarter of the price (25 credits instead of 100), wood, leather and metal together; after that, full price. The screen shows the price of your next one. The store never sells more scrap than it has, and your pouch must have room (100 of each kind per pouch level). The store gets 5 scrap every hour. Scrap can't be sold back.
  • Crafting materials (for Hack & Slash) have no fixed price: the fewer the store has, the dearer they are (the table below). Each one you buy costs the price at the stock left, so buying several costs more than the shown price × the amount, and the next price goes up; selling raises the stock and lowers the price. The screen always shows the next one's price. Selling back what you just bought pays exactly 75% of what you paid (never more). At most 10,000 in one purchase or sale, and the store doesn't buy a material it already has more than 1,000,000 of. The store gets 3 random materials every 3 hours, and from players' sales.
  • The price can move while you look: if another player buys a crafting material first, yours costs the price at the stock left after theirs. The message after your purchase always says what you paid.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Sell what you don't need: most items sell for 75% of their price, more with a Trade Post.
  • Buy up to 5 scrap a day: those cost a quarter of the price.
  • Crafting materials are cheapest when the store has many: after a delivery, or after other players sold theirs. Buying the last few is expensive.

docs.title: 🧱 Super stakers
docs.text:
A super staker is a Runebase wallet that stakes for others: holders delegate their RUNES to it, and it produces blocks with their weight. Register yours with the bot and the server can see how reliably it produces blocks: every 8 hours it earns a point if it did, and a reliable one with delegations holds the super staker role.

Open it from /start → Activities → Super Stakers.

docs.title: The list
docs.text:
Super Stakers lists every registered super staker that is verified (one still waiting for its verification isn't listed): its address, its owner, its delegates, its score (its points out of its cycles, as a percentage: 3 points in 4 cycles is 75% (3/4)) and the blocks it produced. How to become a Super Staker and How to Delegate walk you through the wallet's setup.

Pick one in Select a Super Staker to see it on its own: its address, its note and its delegations, 5 a page (each delegate with its weight, fee and the block it started at), with Next and Previous; Back to Super Stakers Overview returns to the list.

docs.title: Registering yours
docs.text:
1. My Super Staker → Register Super Staker Address, and type your super staker's address. An address the Runebase node calls invalid is refused ("You entered an invalid address!"), and nothing is registered.
  2. The screen then asks you to verify it: send any amount of RUNES from that address to the deposit address it shows (your own deposit address, the same as Pouch → Buy Credits).
  3. Only a payment from the super staker's address verifies it; one from any other address doesn't. Once it's verified the bot tells you by DM, and your super staker is in the list.

The RUNES you sent aren't lost: like any deposit, they become credits in your wallet at 6 confirmations.

docs.title: Your note, and disabling it
docs.text:
On My Super Staker, Edit Note opens a box with your super staker's public note; what you save is shown with it in the list. Disable Super Staker asks first (Cancel keeps it); once you confirm, it leaves the list and you can register an address again.

When nothing could be saved, My Super Staker says why, under the screen as it is: you already have a super staker (registered from another screen), your super staker was disabled since the screen was drawn (so there's no note to edit), or the bot couldn't save it (try again later).

docs.title: A point every 8 hours
docs.text:
At 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC every verified super staker gets a cycle, and a point if it produced a block in the last 8 hours. Your score is your points out of your cycles. Each cycle counts once: should the cycle ever run twice within the same 8 hours, the second run counts nothing and posts nothing.

The results are posted in the server's experience channel: who earned a point, who failed to produce a block in the past 8 hours, and who got or lost the role.

docs.title: The super staker role
docs.text:
At each cycle:

  • You get the role when your super staker has at least one delegation and produced a block within the last 72 hours.
  • You lose it when it has no delegations left, or produced no block for more than 72 hours.

So a super staker that stops producing blocks keeps the role for 3 days, but gets no points meanwhile; one whose delegators all left loses it at the next cycle.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep your super staker's wallet online and staking: every 8 hours without a block is a cycle without a point.
  • Verify from the super staker's own address: a payment from any other address does nothing for the verification (it's still credited as a deposit).

docs.title: 🗳️ Votes
docs.text:
A vote for the bot on discordbotlist.com pays 20 experience, a roll on the vote prize table and the voter role for 12 hours. Another vote within those 12 hours pays nothing. A voter who isn't in the server gets nothing; a member who never used the bot gets an account and the reward.

The prize table is without utilities (a 🪓 Wood Axe, 🔪 Skinning Knife or ⛏️ Mining Pick raises the scrap rows; they come last, so a utility never takes anything from the other prizes). Every row of this table is played in the tests and pays exactly what it shows.

Prize Chance per vote 5 to 15 credits 8% 1 Nail 2% 1 Rope 0.4% 1 Engraving Tool 5% 1 Chaos Relic 5% 1 Common Pet Token 1% 1 📦 Pet Token (Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical) 0.5% each 1 Leather Scrap 25% 1 Metal Scrap 25% 1 Wood Scrap 25% nothing 1.1%

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Vote every 12 hours: each vote pays 20 experience and a roll on the vote prize table.

docs.title: 🎫 Games
docs.text:
Every game of Runebase World, each on its own page; each page says where you can play it. How they connect: the guide's first page.

Game What it is 👹 Hack & Slash the role-playing game: quick battles, the Jotnar world boss, the Arena, gear and the auction house Crown of Chaos one player holds the Crown, everyone else attacks it with Chaos Relics; a reign pays the Crown pool Heists and clans steal experience from other players, join a clan, climb the monthly ladder Fishing trips on energy that catch fish, with rods to craft and enhance 🏹 Hunting trips on energy that catch meat, with rifles to craft and enhance 🧭 Expeditions trips on energy that bring back scrap, crafting materials and credits Cooking the fire and the cooking table: fish and meat become dishes that buff the other games 🎰 Loot Reels free spins every day 🔤 WordWeaver guess a hidden word in six tries ♟️ Chess chess against the bot or another player 🏰 Hnefatafl the Viking board game, against the bot or ranked against other players Dice /roll two dice for experience, a RUNES prize and a prize draw Treasure chests open a chest with a Bronze, Silver or Gold Key 🗝️ Piles and the key hunt grab the piles that appear in the channels; the keys you find score on a monthly ladder Scratch cards scratch a card with a Mystery Card for RUNES, experience, keys and more 🃏 Runes Pattern the whole server's game: mark the words on your card as they appear in the channel

docs.title: ♟️ Chess
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Chess against the bot or against another player. Chess has its own leaderboards (all-time and monthly).

Where: /start → Activities → Chess.

docs.title: Against the bot (Singleplayer)
docs.text:
Chess → Singleplayer: pick your side (white, black or random) and a difficulty, then start the game and play against the bot. Pick your move from the menus or type it (SAN Input); the bot answers each move. A move typed wrong is refused on your board (with the moves you can play) and the bot doesn't move.

The bot is the Stockfish chess engine, at the strength of the difficulty:

Difficulty The bot plays like It looks easy a beginner (rated 800) 3 moves ahead, 0.15 seconds a move medium a strong club player (rated 2100) 11 moves ahead, about 2 seconds a move hard at full strength 30 moves ahead, up to 25 seconds a move

The bot sees the whole game, every move played so far, not only the board as it stands: like a player at the table, it knows when a position has come up before.

Forfeit asks first (Cancel keeps playing); a forfeited game is a loss.

  • Only a win pays: experience, credits and maybe scrap (table below), and chess points on the leaderboards:
Difficulty Experience Chess points easy 15 2 medium 20 3 hard 35 5
  • A loss pays nothing, and neither does a draw or a forfeit. A game is drawn by a stalemate, insufficient material, the fifty-move rule, or the same position a third time (by your move or the bot's), and the screen says which.
  • Only the first 5 wins of a UTC day pay. The next day pays again.
  • A new game can start 3 hours after your last one started.
  • Wins also complete the Chess - Win quests, which pay their own experience and rewards.
  • A win pays once, even when the winning move is clicked twice.
Difficulty Credits (always) Also, each on its own chance easy 15 to 25 credits 1 Leather Scrap 25%, 1 Metal Scrap 25%, 1 Wood Scrap 25% medium 25 to 50 credits 2 Leather Scrap 25%, 2 Metal Scrap 25%, 2 Wood Scrap 25% hard 50 to 85 credits 3 Leather Scrap 25%, 3 Metal Scrap 25%, 3 Wood Scrap 25%

Credits always come; each scrap rolls on its own.

docs.title: Against other players (Multiplayer)
docs.text: A multiplayer game pays nothing: no credits, experience, chess points or quest progress. You play for the game.

docs.title: The challenge
docs.text:
Chess → Multiplayer: pick the member to challenge, then the settings:

  • Public (the board is shown in the server's chess channel, for everyone to watch) or Private (only the two of you see it);
  • Normal (3 minutes a move) or Blitz: a clock for each side, from 5 to 125 minutes.

Challenge User posts the challenge in the chess channel, mentioning you both, with Accept and Decline: only the challenged player can answer. Your screen says it's sent and has Cancel Challenge until they answer, and the way back (Activities Menu, Chess Menu): you can wait elsewhere, and when they accept, that screen shows the game. A challenge nobody answers expires after 5 minutes (the channel and your screen say so). The challenged player can also accept it from View Active Games.

You can't challenge yourself, a bot or someone who isn't in the server, and you can have one open challenge or game with the same player at a time (with other players, as many as you like). Anything refused changes nothing and says why: on your own screen (your menu or your board) for a second click, a move out of turn or a Cancel after the game started; privately under the challenge's message or on a button that isn't yours.

docs.title: Playing
docs.text:
Sides are drawn at random; white moves first. On your turn your screen has your moves: pick a piece and a move and press Execute Move, or type the move into SAN Input (e4, Nf3, O-O, exd6, e8=Q). Castling, en passant and promotion (to any piece) work both ways. A move that breaks the rules, or comes when it isn't your turn, is refused on your board, which says why and stays as it was. Your move shows on your opponent's screen with their moves, and a public game's board in the chess channel follows the game.

Discord lets the bot update your screen through your last click for 15 minutes, and a blitz game can run much longer. After that, a screen in the channel (the menu you challenged from) is still updated; a private one (the board Accept showed you) can't be: open View Active Games to see the board and your moves.

A game ends with a checkmate, a resignation, or in a draw by stalemate, insufficient material (a king against a king and a knight, for example), the fifty-move rule or threefold repetition: the same position a third time in the game ends it in a draw, whoever repeats it. A position is the same when the same pieces stand on the same squares with the same player to move, and the same castling and en passant captures possible (a king that walked out and back has lost its castling, so the position before isn't the same one). Both screens and the public board say how the game ended.

docs.title: Resigning
docs.text: While a game runs, both players' screens have Resign (on your turn and on your opponent's). It asks first: Cancel brings your board back, Yes, resign ends the game at once as a loss for you. Your screen, your opponent's and the public board say who resigned and who won. A resigned game pays nothing, like every multiplayer game. Yes, resign clicked twice, or at the moment your opponent moves or a timer runs out, ends the game once (a second click is told privately that the game is already over).

docs.title: The timers
docs.text:
• 3 minutes a move: when your time is up, the bot plays a random legal move for you, and both screens say so.
  • 12 minutes away (no click of yours for 12 minutes) and you forfeit: your opponent wins, and both screens say so.
  • Blitz: your clock runs only during your turns. When it runs out you lose on time.

Only your own moves count: when your move and the turn timer's random move land at the same moment, your move is played; a timer that fires as the game ends doesn't change the result.

If the bot restarts during your game, a restart never counts against you: the player to move gets a DM and 15 minutes before any timer counts again (a blitz clock is paused through them). A challenge waiting at a restart expires once it's 5 minutes old.

docs.title: Your games and your history
docs.text:
View Active Games lists your challenges and games: pick one to see your board again (your moves on your turn), to wait on (or cancel) a challenge you sent, or to accept one sent to you. It shows at most 25 (Discord's limit for a list): the games in progress first, then the challenges sent to you, then the ones you sent, newest first; with more, the screen says how many you have.

Chess History (in the Chess menu) shows every game you played, single player and multiplayer, as white or black, move by move. Export FEN gives you, privately, the position on the board at the move shown (finished games only).

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Chess pays only 5 wins a day; a hard win pays the most.

docs.title: Cooking
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

The fire and the cooking table turn the fish and meat in your basket, with spices and sauces from the 🏪 store, into dishes: buffs for fishing, hunting, expeditions, the heists, Crown of Chaos and Hack & Slash.

docs.title: The fire and cooking
docs.text:
1. /fire costs one Wood Scrap and starts a fire in the channel for 10 minutes. Starting a fire pays 3 experience and counts on the fire leaderboards. Without wood, or in a channel not every verified member can see and write in, no fire starts, nothing is spent and only you are told why (from Activities → Cooking Fire → Start Fire, the fire guide says it, as public or private as it is).
  2. Add Fuel costs another Wood Scrap, adds 10 minutes and pays 3 experience. Without wood, you're told so privately and nothing is spent.
  3. Cook opens your private cooking table. Pick a recipe and an amount: it uses exactly the recipe's ingredients × the amount from your basket, gives you the dishes, pays 1 experience per dish and moves your cooking quests. Without the ingredients, or with an amount that isn't valid (not a whole number, 0, or more than 5,000 at once), nothing is spent, and the table says why.

The Cuisine Cottage building gives each dish a 1% per level chance of one more; an extra dish pays its experience and counts for your cooking quests like the others. Cooking at two fires at the same moment works: both cooks are paid, and your quests count every dish. A fire that went out while the bot was offline is put out when the bot starts; one whose end the bot missed while running is put out within the hour; its old buttons spend nothing.

docs.title: Dice
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

A quick game of luck: roll two dice for experience, a RUNES prize and a prize draw.

/roll in the dice channel. A roll pays experience by the sum you roll (the rarer the sum, the more), a RUNES prize tipped to you (also by the sum), and one prize draw from the dice prize table (below). Then the dice wait 2 hours (the bot tells you when you can roll again); after that you roll again and are paid again.

  • The RUNES prize is a share of the realm's RUNES wallet at the moment you roll, the percentage in the table below for your sum: with 1,000,000 RUNES in the wallet, a 7 pays 1.6 RUNES and a double six 9.6 RUNES.
  • Each 🌍 realm has its own dice: a roll in one server doesn't start the cooldown in another, and each posts its results in its own dice channel.
  • Every roll's result has a Roll Dice button: anyone can press it to roll their own dice (during your cooldown it rolls nothing and tells you, privately, when you can roll again). You can also roll from /start → Activities → Dice.
  • A roll outside the dice channel answers you privately and posts the result in the dice channel.
  • If the tipbot is offline, the roll says so, only to you, and nothing changes; also when the bot can't read the realm's RUNES wallet (it lost the tipbot for over a minute).
  • When the realm's RUNES wallet holds 1 RUNES or less, the dice still roll: you get the experience and the prize draw, and the cooldown starts, but no RUNES. The result shows the RUNES prize as not paid: the realm's RUNES wallet is empty, its table shows no RUNES, and the dice menu says rolls pay no RUNES for now.
  • The same in a server whose RUNES prizes aren't connected yet (every server but the Runebase server, until after the update): the dice roll and pay everything but RUNES, shown as not paid: RUNES prizes aren't connected in this server yet, and the dice menu says so.
  • Two rolls at the same moment: one is paid, the other gets the cooldown, also from two devices (/roll and the dice menu).
  • The cooldown survives a restart of the bot, and the dice menu always counts down to the time a roll would be refused until.
  • The dice leaderboards count each roll's dice score.

docs.title: 🧭 Expeditions
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

An idle activity: you spend energy, wait while your expedition runs, and come back to what it found. Expeditions bring back scrap, crafting materials and credits. Fishing and 🏹 hunting work the same way.

Where: /start → Activities → Expeditions lets you pick how much energy to spend, and holds the Expedition Buffs menu.

docs.title: How a trip works
docs.text:
1. You choose how much energy to spend. Each energy is 10 seconds of trip, longer with a resource building (see below).
  2. While the trip runs you're busy: you can't start another expedition, fishing trip or hunt until it's over (your expeditions screen tells you that you're already busy and until when, with the way back to the menu). That notice has the expedition's own button: press it once you're free to start it with 1 energy.
  3. Every second of the trip is one roll for its scrap, and one roll on the trip's extra prizes (crafting materials, pet items, tokens, credits and more; the table is at the end of this page).
  4. Each scrap found is its own prize, as in fishing and hunting: when your pouch is full, the scrap that still fits is paid and the rest isn't. The result lists what was paid and, apart, what your pouch had no room for (Unable to loot Pouch full); Today's loot on the menu counts only what was paid (with the trips' experience and quest rewards).
  5. At the end you get what it found, your experience and your quest progress, and the trip counts on the leaderboards.

A trip pays exactly once. Clicking twice, or using two devices, starts one trip and spends the energy once. If the bot restarts during your trip, the trip is finished when the bot is back, and paid once.

docs.text:

  • Energy refills at 00:00 UTC every day. The refill sets your energy to the day's full amount; it doesn't add to what you had left.
  • A trip that runs over midnight still pays once.
  • Expeditions have no dish for more energy (fishing and hunting have one): without expedition energy, expeditions can't be started. If you click an expedition without the energy it needs (say, spent on another device), the menu says so (it shows your energy as it is now) and nothing is spent.

An expedition pays 3 experience per energy.

Expeditions also move your quests: the expedition quests count the seconds of your expeditions. A quest that reaches its goal completes on its own and pays its reward once.

The expedition board counts expedition seconds.
