docs.title: 🏰 Hnefatafl
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

The Viking board game, new in this release, against the bot or against another player. Hnefatafl has its own leaderboards (all-time and monthly).

Where: /start → Activities → Hnefatafl.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
Two sides on an 11 × 11 board (the Copenhagen rules):

  • The attackers (24 pieces) move first and win by surrounding the King on all four sides. A King on the edge of the board can't be captured.
  • The defenders (12 pieces and the King, who starts on the throne in the middle) win when the King reaches a corner.
  • Encirclement: the attackers also win when their move closes a ring around the King and every remaining defender, so that none of them can reach the edge of the board. Pieces move in straight lines, so attackers touching corner to corner close the ring. A ring with a gap, a defender left outside it, or a ring that leaves the King room to reach the edge is no encirclement.
  • Exit fort: the defenders also win when, after their move, the King stands on the edge of the board, can still move, and is walled in by defenders the attackers can never capture: only defenders and the edge around the King's free squares, and every one of those defenders backed (on each line, across and along, at least one neighbour the attackers can never take: the edge, the King's free squares, or another such defender). A wall piece with open squares on both sides of a line, an attacker touching the King's squares, or a King with no free square is no fort. The King inside his fort but off the edge isn't a win yet; back on the edge it is.
  • Pieces move in straight lines, any number of free squares, and can't jump. Only the King may stop on the throne or the corners.
  • A piece is captured when it's sandwiched between two enemies (a corner and the empty throne count as enemies). Moving into a sandwich yourself is safe. A row of defenders along the edge can be captured by a shieldwall.
  • A side with no legal move loses.
  • The same position a third time is a draw: when the same pieces stand on the same squares with the same side to move for the third time in a game (counted over the whole game), the game ends in a draw, whichever side repeats (the published Copenhagen rules make a repetition a loss for the King's side instead). Moving a piece out and back while your opponent does the same ends the game on the 8th such move.
  • A move that breaks the rules is refused: your board says why and stays as it was.

docs.title: Against the bot (Singleplayer)
docs.text:
Hnefatafl → Singleplayer: pick a difficulty and your side (the King's side, the attackers, or random), then start. The attackers move first, so as the King's side you find the bot's opening move already played. Type your moves into Make Move as from-to (f8-f9); the bot answers each one. A move that breaks the rules is refused privately and the board stays.

Difficulty The bot thinks easy 1 move ahead, and picks among its nearly best moves at random medium 2 moves ahead hard 3 moves ahead

Forfeit asks first (Cancel keeps playing); Yes, forfeit ends that game as a loss, once (clicked again, its screen says the game is already over, and it never ends a newer game). A new game can start right away: unlike chess, there's no wait between games.

A win pays credits and maybe scrap, by difficulty (table below); every way of winning counts (the King's escape, a capture, an encirclement, an exit fort, no legal move left). A loss and a forfeit pay nothing. Only the first 5 wins of a UTC day pay; the 6th says so and pays nothing. Hnefatafl gives no experience: its Win quests pay their other rewards. A draw (a position played a third time) pays nothing, counts for no Win quest, and isn't one of your 5 paid wins.

Difficulty Credits (always) Also, each on its own chance easy 15 to 25 credits 1 Leather Scrap 25%, 1 Metal Scrap 25%, 1 Wood Scrap 25% medium 25 to 50 credits 2 Leather Scrap 25%, 2 Metal Scrap 25%, 2 Wood Scrap 25% hard 50 to 85 credits 3 Leather Scrap 25%, 3 Metal Scrap 25%, 3 Wood Scrap 25%

docs.title: The challenge
docs.text:
Hnefatafl → Multiplayer (the lobby): pick your side (random, the King's side or the attackers) and the member to challenge. Your challenge is posted in the server's Hnefatafl channel, mentioning them (no DM), with who plays which side and Accept and Decline, which only they can use; they also find it in their lobby (Refresh) with Accept and Decline; your lobby lists it with Cancel. When they accept or decline, you cancel, or the challenge expires, the post and your lobby say so at once, and the post's buttons go. Accept on the post shows them their board privately, and the game is on. Every challenge in your lobby has its buttons, the ones sent to you first. A challenge nobody answers expires after 30 minutes (a restart gives a waiting challenge a fresh 30 minutes).

A server without a Hnefatafl channel can't take challenges: your lobby says so and nothing is sent (an admin sets the channel with /config, Hnefatafl Channel).

You can't challenge yourself or a bot, and you can have one open challenge or game with the same player at a time. Anything refused changes nothing and says why: on your lobby or your board when the button is on your own screen (a late Accept, a second click, a move from an old screen or typed wrong), privately under the challenge's post in the channel or on a button that isn't yours.

docs.title: How a game ends
docs.text:
The King escapes to a corner, the King is captured, the attackers ring in the King and every defender (encirclement), the King holds an exit fort, the side to move has no legal move, the same position comes a third time (a draw), a player resigns (Resign), or the player to move doesn't move within 15 minutes (they lose). The game then leaves both lobbies.

Resign asks first, on your turn or your opponent's: Cancel brings your board back, Yes, resign ends the game at once as a loss for you, and both screens say so. Yes, resign clicked twice ends the game once (the second click's screen says the game is over), and a Yes, resign left from an earlier game never ends a newer one.

docs.title: Your screen follows the game
docs.text:
Challenges, moves and endings come without a DM (only the notice after a restart still does). Instead, your Hnefatafl message follows the game: the board you last looked at, or your lobby if you haven't opened the game. When your opponent moves, it shows their move and, on your turn, your Make Move; when the game ends (a move, a resignation, a timeout), both players' messages show the result, with a note when the game scored no ranked points. Leave Multiplayer for the Hnefatafl menu or Singleplayer and that message is left alone; your lobby shows your games when you come back.

Discord lets the bot update a message through your last click for 15 minutes. After that, a message in the channel is still updated; a private one can't be (open your lobby to see the game). The board Accept on the post showed you is private.

docs.title: Ranked points
docs.text:
Multiplayer games score ranked points on the Hnefatafl leaderboards: 25 for a win, 5 for a loss, 12 each for a draw. To stop farming:

  • a game only scores when both sides made at least 10 moves (a game resigned in its first moves scores nothing);
  • the same two players score at most 3 ranked games a day (another opponent still scores);
  • a player scores at most 5 ranked games a day, whoever the opponents are;
  • you can't challenge yourself.

A draw comes from playing the same position a third time (see the rules above), and scores 12 each, once.

The boards: /leaderboard → All-Time Hnefatafl Points or Monthly Hnefatafl Points, best first.

Only the side to move may move, each player from their own screen; a move sent from a second Make Move after yours is refused (it isn't your turn), and so is a move sent after the game ended. A move and a resignation at the same moment end the game once and score once. An abandoned game times out once, within the same limits. A restart never counts against you: as in ♟️ chess, the player to move gets a DM and 15 minutes.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Hnefatafl pays only 5 wins a day; a hard win pays the most.

docs.title: 🏹 Hunting
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

An idle activity: you spend energy, wait while your trip runs, and come back to a catch. Hunting fills your basket with meat for cooking. Fishing and 🧭 expeditions work the same way.

Where: /hunt goes on a one-energy trip straight away. /start → Activities → Hunt lets you pick how much energy to spend, and holds the crafting, equipment and buff menus.

docs.title: How a trip works
docs.text:
1. You choose how much energy to spend. Each energy is 10 seconds of trip.
  2. While the trip runs you're busy: you can't start another hunt, fishing trip or expedition until it's over (the bot tells you that you're already busy and until when: privately after /hunt, on the menu after its button).
  3. Every second of the trip is one roll for a catch, and one roll on the trip's extra prizes (scrap, pet items, tokens and more; the table is at the end of this page).
  4. Each scrap found is its own prize: when your pouch is full, the scrap that still fits is paid and the rest isn't. The result lists what was paid and, apart, what your pouch had no room for (Unable to loot Pouch full); Today's loot on the hunting menu counts only what was paid (with the trips' experience and quest rewards).
  5. At the end you get your catch, your experience and your quest progress, and the trip counts on the leaderboards.

A trip pays exactly once. Clicking twice, or using two devices, starts one trip and spends the energy once. If the bot restarts during your trip, the trip is finished when the bot is back, and paid once.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Activity Energy each day Most energy Seconds per energy Hunting 10 + Hunting Cabin level 22 (level 12, rank 96) 10 (+2 per Hunting Weed)
  • Energy refills at 00:00 UTC every day. The refill sets your energy to the day's full amount; it doesn't add to what you had left.
  • A trip that runs over midnight still pays once.
  • Out of hunting energy? A Wild Boar with Cherry Sauce pays for one more energy of hunting. It's only used for the energy your daily energy doesn't cover, never while you still have energy. Without one, the trip doesn't start and nothing is spent: /hunt tells you so privately, with your hunting menu (your energy, when it refills), and a Go Hunting button on a menu from earlier tells you privately and leaves the menu as it was.

docs.title: Experience, quests and leaderboards
docs.text:
A hunt pays 1 experience per energy.

Trips also move your quests: the Hunting quest counts the energy you spend, and the quest for each animal counts what you catch of it (Hunting - Elk counts your elk). A quest that reaches its goal completes on its own and pays its reward once.

The hunting leaderboards count the seconds of your trips (weed seconds included).

You craft them in the Hunt menu (Craft Hunting Rifle) for scrap from your pouch. You can own one of each. Without one, you only catch Squirrel.

  • With more than one rifle you can turn on rotative hunting: each second of the trip rolls on the next one in turn. With only one, the switch isn't offered and a trip never rotates.

docs.text:
Buff Where it comes from Used by Hunting Weed 3 credits in the store; the Party Store hunting Wild Boar with Cherry Sauce cooked: 2 Wild Boar + 6 Cherry Sauce hunting, when the energy is gone
  • Hunting Weed (bought from the store, or collected at the Party Store): each one adds 2 seconds to one energy of a trip, so a trip uses one per energy, at most. A 3-energy trip with 2 weeds lasts 34 seconds. The extra seconds roll for catches and extra prizes like any other second, and count on the leaderboard. Experience and the Hunting quest count energy, so the extra seconds add none.
  • The hunting menu shows the buffs you have and the trip time they give.

docs.title: Pets
docs.text: Your active pet helps while it's awake and cared for (see 🐾 Pets for every pet, its perks and when they work). Its hunting perk adds its points to one animal. A perk for an animal your rifle doesn't hunt does nothing: a Moose perk needs the Weatherby Mark V, and without a rifle only a Squirrel perk helps. Asleep, or below the perk's conditions, the pet adds nothing. The pet counts if it's active and awake when the trip ends: a pet changed during the trip gives its perks, one put to sleep gives none.

docs.title: Buildings that help
docs.text:
In 🏗️ Buildings: the Hunting Cabin gives +1 hunting energy a day per level.

Everything adds up once: a rifle enhancement, a pet perk, weed and the Hunting Cabin on one trip each count exactly once.

docs.text:

  • A rifle's enhancement only helps its own three animals.

docs.title: 🗝️ Piles and the key hunt
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Be first to grab the piles that appear in the server's channels, and climb the monthly key hunt with the treasure keys you find. Keys open treasure chests.

docs.title: Piles
docs.text:
Piles of credits, treasure keys, scrap and building supplies appear in the server's channels for a short time, in every 🌍 realm: each server gets every kind of pile on the same schedule, in channels its verified members can see. What you collect goes to your account in that server (its pouch, its quests and boards, its key hunt and its 4-hour key windows). To collect one, press its button and answer the captcha: the first players to answer correctly take the pile's slots.

  • Credit piles are shared: each collector gets their share. Answering the captcha wrong, or collecting twice, pays nothing.
  • A wrong answer shows the captcha again, marked incorrect: press Answer again for another try.
  • Discord shows you one captcha at a time: a captcha you closed without answering doesn't count, and your next answer goes to the pile you answered, once.
  • A pile still open when the bot restarts stays collectable until its time is up.
  • A pile has a limited number of slots: when more players answer than there are slots, only the first ones are paid, and the others are told.
  • When a credit pile expires, its unclaimed share goes to the Crown of Chaos pool.
  • A key or supply pile taken to its last slot is replaced by a post naming who collected it, with a Pouch (keys, scrap) or Basket (building supplies) button: whoever clicks it sees their own pouch or basket, privately; the post stays as it is.
  • Nail piles come every hour: each of their players gets the same number of Nails (3 to 9, set when the pile appears) and 2 experience.
  • Treasure keys: the first key of each type you find in 4 hours pays 10 experience. Within those 4 hours, your 6th Bronze Key, 4th Silver Key or 2nd Gold Key also gives a Mystery Card. Each type counts on its own, and its 4 hours start with its first key; the message for each key you find says when they end and how many more you need for the card. A restart of the bot, even in the middle of your find, never pays those 10 experience twice and never loses them.

When they come, how long they stay and what they hold:

Pile boards (/leaderboard): the Scrap, Credits Pile and BuildingSupply Pile Collector boards, all-time and monthly, count 1 for each pile you collect, whatever it held. The TreasureKey Finder board counts 1 for each key.

docs.title: Key hunt
docs.text:
The Monthly TreasureKey Hunt Ladder (/leaderboard, monthly boards) ranks the treasure key hunters of the calendar month, each server its own (a key found in a server counts toward that server's ladder): each key you find scores 1 point for a Bronze Key, 2 for a Silver Key, 3 for a Gold Key. When the staff pay the monthly prizes (on the Runebase server), last month's best hunters share 0.75% of the realm's RUNES wallet by rank:

Rank Shares of the pool, each 1 12 2 10 3 8 4 to 5 5 6 to 10 3 11 to 25 1.5 26 to 50 0.75

A tie goes to whoever found their keys first, and players who left the server are left out.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Piles go fast: answer the captcha quickly.

docs.title: 🃏 Runes Pattern
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

A game for the whole server in the Runes Pattern channel. A word appears in the channel every 20 seconds; click the ones on your card to mark them.

  • A word that isn't on your card is a penalty: it costs you one marking.
  • The word that completes the day's current challenge (a pattern on the card) wins the game: the winner uses one Runes Pattern Card and is paid once (experience and a prize roll), and a new game starts. When two players click the winning word at the same moment, there is one winner.
  • A win pays 50 experience; the day's 3rd challenge pays 150 and counts the day toward the weekly challenge.
  • The challenges follow the UTC day.
  • Words disappear from the channel when their time is up. No word comes twice until all 75 have come; then the channel says the word pool starts over.
  • Show My Runes Pattern Card (under every word) or Activities → Runes Pattern shows your own card, only to you: your words, what you've marked, today's challenges and the week's. Your card is dealt the first time you look at it or click a word.
  • Every click on a word is answered only to you: marked, already marked, not on your card, or expired. A word clicked twice at once is marked once. Without a Runes Pattern Card a click marks nothing and offers the store.
  • The wild card: the word Runes is a wild card. Collect it (once per word) and your card shows Apply Wild Card: pick any unmarked word of your card and it's marked. A wild card that completes the challenge wins like a word, with one Runes Pattern Card. Your wild card stays yours when the word you picked was marked meanwhile, or when you have no Runes Pattern Card left (the bot tells you); picked on two devices at once, it's used once.
  • Users Playing lists who plays (20 a page); players who chose to play anonymously show as "Anonymous Player". A player who hasn't clicked for 15 minutes leaves the list.
  • If something goes wrong with a click, you are told (only you, under a word; on your card or its screen otherwise) and nothing is marked or used: click again. Apply Wild Card and its position menu work on your card's own message: without a wild card, or with every position already marked, your card says so and no wild card is used.

Runes Pattern Cards cost 50 credits in the 🏪 store; they also drop from many prize tables.

docs.title: Scratch cards
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

/scratchcard in the scratch card channel. A card costs one Mystery Card (a scratch credit, from your pouch). Scratch all three fields, then Collect: the card pays its combination once.

  • RUNES prizes are a share of the realm's RUNES wallet, sent to you as a tip. Other prizes go to your pouch, your basket or your experience (a Gold Key, a Runes Pattern Card, a new Mystery Card…).
  • Scratch cards are dealt in every 🌍 realm (every server the bot plays in), from the Mystery Cards of that server's pouch; their RUNES prizes come from that server's own RUNES wallet (the odds show them from it), and none when it's empty.
  • No card is dealt without a Mystery Card, outside the scratch card channel, on a server whose admins haven't set a scratch card channel, or when you already have 100 cards open (the bot says so, and your Mystery Card is kept). Every refusal is told only to you.
  • /scratchcard and Scratch again answer at once, even when the bot is busy: in the scratch card channel you see the bot thinking, then your card; a refusal replaces that with a note only you see.
  • Activities → Scratch Card shows your Mystery Cards and the odds; New Scratch Card deals a card right there, to scratch and collect on the menu. Under a card you collected in the channel, Scratch again deals your next one. When the menu can't deal a card (no Mystery Card left, 100 cards open, the tipbot offline, no scratch card channel on the server), only you are told why and your menu stays as it was.
  • A card's buttons are its owner's: anyone else pressing them is told, only to them, that it isn't their card.
  • A card waits for you when the bot restarts: scratch the rest and collect it afterwards; it pays once.
  • If the tipbot is offline (also when the bot can't read the realm's RUNES wallet), no card is dealt and your Mystery Card is kept. If it goes offline before you press Collect, you are told (on the menu, or only you under a card in the channel), the card waits, and it pays once when the tipbot is back.
  • When the realm's RUNES wallet holds 1 RUNES or less, cards are still dealt and collected: the odds show the RUNES combinations as no RUNES, and such a card pays nothing, shown as not paid: the realm's RUNES wallet is empty.
  • The same in a server whose RUNES prizes aren't connected yet (every server but the Runebase server, until after the update): the odds show the RUNES combinations as no RUNES: RUNES prizes aren't connected in this server yet, and such a card pays nothing, shown as not paid.
  • A card pays once, also when it's shown twice (in the channel and in Activities → Scratch Card) or a field is clicked twice: a field scratches once, and a collected card pays nothing more.
  • Collect before all three fields are scratched tells you to scratch them first (on the menu, or only you under a card in the channel).
  • The result shows the prize with the combination's chance per card, as in the table below. Every combination is played in the tests and pays exactly what it shows.
  • A prize your pouch has no room for isn't paid, and the result says so. FRE and AES give one of each key: a key whose pouch is full isn't paid, the others are, and the result names each key.
  • If something goes wrong while you collect, scratch or get a card, you are told (on the menu, or only you under a card in the channel), nothing is spent or paid, and the card waits for you: collect or scratch again. In the menu, no Mystery Card or 100 open cards are said on the menu too.

Mystery Cards come from the Party Store, heists, chests, 🎰 Loot Reels, 🗝️ treasure key finds (the 6th Bronze, 4th Silver or 2nd Gold Key within 4 hours of your first of that kind) and other prize tables. The HUG combination also gives 1 experience.

docs.title: Treasure chests
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

A quick game of luck: open treasure chests with keys.

/treasurechest in the treasure chest channel shows the chest. Loot treasure chest, then pick a key: the chest spends exactly that key and rolls its key's prize table three times ( credits, RUNES, items, experience). A chest whose three rolls all miss pays 1 experience.

  • Without that key, or with the tipbot offline (also when the bot can't read the realm's RUNES wallet), nothing is spent: only you are told.
  • When the realm's RUNES wallet holds 1 RUNES or less, chests still open: the loot table shows its RUNES rows as none: the realm's RUNES wallet is empty, and a RUNES prize you roll is shown as not paid (0 RUNES); the key is spent and the rest of the chest is paid.
  • The same in a server whose RUNES prizes aren't connected yet (every server but the Runebase server, until after the update): the loot table shows its RUNES rows as none: RUNES prizes aren't connected in this server yet, and a RUNES prize is shown as not paid; the rest of the chest is paid.
  • One key clicked on two chest buttons at once opens one chest and spends the key once, also when one of them is in Activities → Treasure and the other under a chest in the channel.
  • Activities → Treasure opens the same chests from the menu: pick a key's table (View … Loot Table), then Use … key; the result shows on your menu and in the chest channel. Without that key, or with the tipbot offline, your menu says why and nothing is spent.
  • Chests open in every 🌍 realm (every server the bot plays in), with the keys of that server's pouch: with /treasurechest only in the server's chest channel, from Activities → Treasure in any channel. Their RUNES prizes come from that server's own RUNES wallet (the loot table shows them from it), and none when it's empty. A server whose admins haven't set a chest channel opens no chests: the bot tells you so (only you, or on your menu from Activities → Treasure), and nothing is spent. Every refusal of /treasurechest or of a chest in the channel is told only to you: no chest channel on the server, the wrong channel (also on a chest posted before the chest channel moved), no key, or a key button pressed faster than the bot allows; from Activities → Treasure your menu says why.

docs.title: 🔤 WordWeaver
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Guess a hidden word of 5 to 8 letters. WordWeaver has its own leaderboards (all-time and monthly).

Where: /start → Activities → WordWeaver.

  1. Get new word deals the word.
  2. Guess Word opens a box to type your guess. You have six guesses: after the sixth wrong one the game is over and pays nothing, and a seventh is refused. A word that doesn't exist is refused and doesn't cost a guess.
  3. Solving the word pays 20 experience, a prize from the table below and one point on the WordWeaver leaderboards. It pays once; an old Guess button pays nothing.
  4. Each solved word counts 1 toward the WordWeaver - Solved quest (a wrong guess counts nothing). A solve that completes it shows the quest's rewards with the word's and pays them once, the quest's experience on top of the 20.

A new word comes 4 hours after your last one was dealt.

docs.text: • A word that doesn't exist costs nothing, so try a real word that tests many letters.

docs.title: Crown of Chaos
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

One player in the realm holds the Crown. The Crown earns a point every minute it holds on; everyone else spends Chaos Relics to attack it. When the Crown's health reaches 0, the reign ends: the old Crown is paid the realm's Crown pool in credits, a RUNES reward and experience, and the next Crown is drawn from the attackers, weighted by their points.

Where: /start → Activities → Crown Of Chaos. The menu shows the Crown, its health, the pool ("Accumulated Crown Tax", also on the attack screen and in the store), your buffs, and the buttons to attack, pick runes, learn skills and eat buffs. The Crown also sees its own skills there. Under the attack reports and round messages in the Crown of Chaos channel, anyone can press Attack The Crown (their own attack screen), Attack Score Board or CoC Weekly Ladder: each answers only the player who pressed it.

docs.title: How a reign works
docs.text:
• A server's very first reign goes to a random player of the server: someone with an account (players get one with their first chat message) who is still a member, never a bot. It starts behind a 90-minute seizure bubble, and "A new era begins!" is posted. In a new server where nobody has an account yet, the first Crown is drawn at the first minute's round after someone has one. A restart never starts a new reign while one is running.
  • When a reign ends and nobody who attacked it is still in the server, the next Crown is drawn among the server's players the same way, never the Crown that just fell (the end of a reign).
  • A new Crown starts with its full health and a seizure bubble of 30 minutes: nobody can attack until it runs out, or until the new Crown removes it (Remove Bubble). Attacks against a bubble spend nothing.
  • Every minute (a round) the Crown gets 1 point, regenerates a little, and bleeds and seeds on it run (📊 the round).
  • The longer a Crown holds on, the more damage it takes (the handicap: 📊 the round).
  • The reign ends when an attack or a round brings the Crown's health to 0, or when the Crown leaves the server.
  • A restart of the bot keeps the reign as it was: the Crown and its role, its bleeds, bubble and silence, the attackers' mana and cooldowns.

The Crown's numbers before any skills, buildings, pets and buffs:

Before skills, buildings, pets and buffs Value The Crown's maximum health 1,000 Regeneration 1 health every 5 points Cooldown on each attacker after an attack 15 s Dodge 0% Resurgence 3% of the maximum health a round for 10 rounds; cooldown 1 hour Blood Purge cooldown 20 minutes Defuse cooldown 15 minutes Mana Drain 10% of the attacker's maximum mana a hit, for 5 minutes; cooldown 45 minutes Bubble 5 minutes; cooldown 1 hour Tax pile on a hit 5% chance, 1% of the pool Tax pile on a round 10% chance, 3% of the pool An attacker's mana 1,000, +10 a round

docs.text: Page What you'll find 🤺 Attacking the Crown Chaos Relics, cooldowns, runes and damage, mana and attack skills 👑 Holding the Crown the Crown's own skills, defensive runes, buildings 🌀 Skills skill points and resets, a page per skill 🧪 Buffs the two Crown of Chaos dishes and their charges 📊 The round and the reign the minute round, points, the end of a reign, the pool 🪜 The weekly ladder the weekly score, the winners role, the RUNES payout

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: An attack that completes the Damage Dealt quest pays its experience (25) to the attacker, and a round that completes the Crown's Points Earned quest pays the Crown its experience (65), on top of anything else.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Watch the attack reports: they show the Crown's rune and its value, so you can pick the rune with the most steps above it (the one valued just below the Crown's).
  • Bleeds and seeds keep earning you points every round; Blood Purge and Defuse are the Crown's answers.
  • As the Crown, cycle several defensive runes so attackers can't read your next one, and save Bubble and Resurgence for heavy attacks.
  • Keep your mana for the skill that matters: only the skill you pick costs mana.

docs.title: 🤺 Attacking the Crown
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Attack The Crown, pick an offensive rune (each option shows its value in this reign) and, if you like, an attack skill, then attack.

  • Each attack costs one Chaos Relic (2 credits in the store; you can also Buy Chaos Relic from the Crown of Chaos menu, and 5% of what you pay goes into the pool). Without a relic the attack button is off. A double click spends one relic once.
  • Then you wait for the cooldown before your next attack (the bot says "Attack Cooldown"; nothing is spent). The cooldown is the Crown's 15 s, plus the Crown's Fractured Time and Temporal Nexus, minus your Blood Rush, and never under 3 seconds.
  • The Crown can't attack itself.

docs.title: Runes and damage
docs.text:
In a reign, each of the 24 runes has a value from 1 to 24 (the menus and the attack reports show it). Every reign draws new values: when a new Crown takes over, the 24 values are shuffled again, so a rune that was strong last reign may be weak now. The Crown has a current defensive rune, and every attack faces it:

  • Your damage comes from how many steps your rune's value is above the Crown's rune's value (a value of 24 against 14 is 10 steps; 24 against 22 is 2): 3 damage per step.
  • The counting goes on past 24 and starts again at 1, so a rune valued below the Crown's still hits: 9 against 10 is 23 steps, the most there is, and 3 against 10 is 17.
  • The same value misses: "The crown defended without taking damage!" The relic is still spent.
  • After every attack (a hit, a miss or a dodge) the Crown's rune moves on to the next one in its list. Each public attack report shows both runes with their values.
  • On top of the steps come your extra damage ( Brutal Strike, the White-tailed Deer 🧪 buff, 🐾 pets), less the Crown's damage reduction (the Blackened Tilapia 🧪 buff, pets), multiplied by the Crown's handicap. A pet's perks count only while it's awake and well cared for (🐾 Pets): the challenge screen shows your pet's extra damage range and attack cooldown reduction (you wait the Crown's cooldown less it), and every pet's attacking perks are checked in play at those numbers.
  • The Crown can dodge ( Veil of Shadows, pets): a dodged attack deals nothing but still costs the relic.

docs.title: Mana and attack skills
docs.text:
You have 1,000 mana, and you get 10 back every round (more with Abyssal Mana Tide), up to 1,000. Only the attack skill you pick costs mana, once. Without enough mana, the attack goes on without the skill and costs no mana.

  • Brutal Strike: extra damage on the hit.
  • Bleed: on a hit, the Crown bleeds for some rounds; each round's bleed damage counts as your damage. A new bleed of yours replaces your old one.
  • Doomseed: on a hit, plants a seed that detonates after its rounds (fewer with Premature Bloom); Thornburst gives a detonation a chance to make the Crown bleed too (not a detonation the Crown's Bubble absorbs). A new seed of yours replaces your old one, and its rounds start again.
  • Robin Hood: on a damaging hit, steals a share of the pool and splits it evenly among the reign's attackers still in the server (everyone who attacked this reign, a miss too, but not players who have left the server; nobody gets anything when the share would be under one unit each). Black Hood: steals a share for you alone. Each steals exactly its share; the rounding remainder stays in the pool.
  • Silence: on a hit, the Crown can't use Resurgence, Blood Purge, Defuse or Mana Drain for the silence's duration (Bubble still works).

docs.title: 🧪 Crown of Chaos buffs
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Eat them in Crown Buffs; each one you eat is a charge (at most 500 held). One charge is used on every attack, whether it hits, misses or is dodged; none when the attack bounces off a bubble or waits for a cooldown. The Crown Buffs screen shows the charges you hold.

Buff Effect, per charge Cooked from Blackened Tilapia with Cumin Slaw 15 less damage from an attack on you as the Crown 2 Tilapia + 6 Cumin White-tailed Deer with Juniper Berry Demi-Glace +15 damage on your attack 2 White-tailed Deer + 2 Juniper Berry Demi-Glace

docs.title: 👑 Holding the Crown
docs.text: Where to play: Discord

docs.title: The Crown's skills
docs.text:
Only the Crown has these buttons. They cost nothing but their cooldown; clicking one again while it cools down changes nothing. When one can't be used (it cools down, there's nothing to remove, the Crown is silenced), your Crown of Chaos menu says why, and nothing changes.

Skill What it does Resurgence heals 3% of the maximum health each of the next 10 rounds, never above the maximum; then waits an hour Blood Purge removes every bleed on the Crown, whoever cast it (seeds stay). With no bleed on the Crown it's refused (your menu says why) and stays ready Defuse removes every seed waiting to detonate. With none, it's refused ("No detonations to defuse", on your menu) and stays ready Mana Drain while it lasts, every hit on the Crown (not a miss) drains 10% of the attacker's mana, never below 0 Bubble while it lasts, attacks bounce off for free, bleeds on the Crown deal 0 but still run down, and a seed that detonates deals nothing and starts no Thornburst bleed (it's used up, and nothing of it hits after the Bubble). Remove Bubble ends it early. Then it waits an hour

Their base cooldowns and durations are on the overview; what the defensive skills change, on their pages.

docs.title: Checked in play
docs.text:
• Resurgence: Heals 3% of the maximum health each of the next 10 rounds (30 at 1,000; 33 with Throne of Endurance 1; 90 with Throne 20), never above it. Ready again in an hour, and the answer says when; +20 on the weekly ladder.
  • Blood Purge: Removes every bleed, whoever cast it, and leaves the seeds; +5 a bleed it removed. Then it waits 1,200 s, less Urgent Embind's 45 s a rank, and its answer says until when. With no bleed on the Crown it's refused, on the Crown's menu, and stays ready. A bleed that has ticked its last round is gone at once, and Hemostasis keeps one with no rounds from being put on; one with no rounds left from an older reign counts for nothing (refused when it's the only one).
  • Defuse: Removes every seed, whoever planted it, and leaves the bleeds; +5 a seed it removed. Then it waits 900 s, less Swift Disarmament's 30 s a rank, and its answer says until when. With no seed it's refused, on the Crown's menu, and stays ready. A seed is gone once it detonates; one left from an older reign with no rounds counts for nothing (refused when it's the only one).
  • Mana Drain: For 300 s (plus Siphon's Grasp) each hit drains 10% of the attacker's 1,000 mana after the skill's own mana, never more than is left (the message says what it took); a miss or a dodge drains nothing. +2 a drained hit, also one that found no mana left. Ready again after 45 minutes.
  • Bubble: For 300 s every attack bounces off, whatever its skill: no relic, mana, buff charge or cooldown spent, nothing applied or stolen, nothing on the weekly ladder. The round goes on under it: bleeds and seeds deal 0 and run down (a seed is spent, no Thornburst), regeneration, a Resurgence, mana, points and tax piles go on. +15; ready again in an hour; Remove Bubble ends it.
  • Silenced: When an attacker's Silence lands, Resurgence, Blood Purge, Defuse and Mana Drain are refused (the Crown's menu says why), even from an old button, and stay ready; a Resurgence or Mana Drain already running goes on; the Bubble works.

docs.title: Defensive runes
docs.text: In Defensive Runes, pick up to 24 runes (the first becomes your current rune), move them up or down, and set the current one. Each line shows the rune's value in the running reign. While you hold the Crown, each attack faces your current rune and then moves it to the next in your list. A change you make while an attack is under way waits for that attack and is kept. Each attack report shows the Crown's defense streak (the attacks it has survived this reign), and your best streak is kept.

docs.title: Pets
docs.text: Your active pet's holding perks count while you hold the Crown, it's awake and its stats meet the perks' conditions (🐾 Pets): extra maximum health (flat or %), more health regenerated every 5th point (or every 4th with the Shadow Hound), a dodge chance, less damage from each hit, a longer wait for each attacker, a stronger Resurgence (the Phoenix Chick: 4.25% a round). The Crown menu shows each with its number, and a new reign starts at your maximum health with your pet's bonus. Asleep, they add nothing; your pet's attacking perks don't help you hold the Crown. Checked in play for every pet.

docs.title: Buildings
docs.text: 🏗️ Buildings help the Crown: Bastion of the Chosen (+15 maximum health per level), Pillar of the Undying (every 5th point heals 1 + 3 per level) and Temporal Nexus (+1 second per level on each attacker's cooldown). A new Crown with Throne of Endurance starts with 1,000 × (1 + 10% per rank) health.

docs.title: 📊 The round and the reign
docs.text: Where to play: Discord

docs.title: The round, every minute
docs.text:
• The Crown gets 1 point: on the reign, on the Crown of Chaos leaderboards (all-time and monthly, with their top-10 roles) and on the weekly ladder. Every 5th point it regenerates health.
  • Every attacker's points shrink by 0.35%, and every attacker gets mana back.
  • Bleeds and seeds on the Crown run; their damage counts for whoever cast them. A bleed or a detonation can end the reign.
  • Sometimes the round drops a tax pile (3% of the pool) in the Crown of Chaos channel, collected like a credit pile. A hit can drop one too (1% of the pool). Each tax pile is for 3, 4 or 5 players (drawn for each pile, the pile says how many), who get equal shares, rounded down; what the rounding leaves over stays in the pool. An empty pool drops no pile.
  • The handicap: once the first 30 minutes of a reign are over, every round adds 1000% ÷ 10,080 to the Crown's handicap (up to 1,000% after 7 days), and every attack's damage is multiplied by (1 + handicap). A former Crown's handicap shrinks at a quarter of that speed, until it's gone. Handicap List on the Crown of Chaos menu shows everyone's handicap, ten players a page (Next, Previous). The attack report (and a bleed's or seed's message) shows the extra damage: none when nothing was dealt (a dodge, a miss, or a hit the Bubble absorbed). The handicaps are reset once a week: on Monday at 00:00 UTC (or, if the bot was down then, when it starts again that week).

docs.title: Points
docs.text: Your points in a reign are the damage you dealt (bleeds and detonations included), shrinking a little every round. The final blow adds 200 points. The Attack Score Board ranks the attackers by points (and shows their damage), ten a page (Next, Previous): that's the order of the draw for the next Crown and of the top-three RUNES shares.

docs.title: The end of a reign
docs.text:
When an attack or a round's bleed brings the Crown to 0:

  1. The next Crown is drawn among everyone with points in this reign who is still in the server: each player's chance is exactly their share of all the points. The draw is posted with its roll and each player's range (300 points of 750 is "0.00-299.99", the next player's starts at 300.00, and so on); a player with 0 points has no chance. The final blow's 200 points help, but don't crown you by themselves. When nobody who attacked the reign is still here, the next Crown is drawn among the server's players instead: someone with an account who is still a member, never a bot and never the Crown that just fell, behind the usual seizure bubble; the channel says so. If nobody in the server can take it yet, the channel says so too, and a reign starts at the first minute's round after someone can.
  2. The old Crown gets the whole pool in credits, once (the one prize not capped at 25,000 credits). The pool starts again at 0.
  3. RUNES (a share of the realm's RUNES wallet, tipped): the old Crown gets 0.000032407% per point, counting at most 19,999 points; the final blow gets 3.5% of that while still in the server (a bleed or seed of a player who left can land it: their share stays in the wallet, and the end result says so), and the top three by points still in the server 5%, 3.5% and 1.5% of it (someone who left the server gets no share, and the next one moves up).
  4. Experience: the old Crown gets 0.85 × its points, at most 8,999; a quest completed in the same round (Points Earned) pays its experience on top (a 1,000-point reign: 850 + the quest's 65; an 11,000-point reign: 8,999 + 65).

  5. The Crown role moves to the new Crown, who starts with a seizure bubble.

  6. Two final blows at the same moment (a round and an attack, two attackers, a double click) end the reign once and pay the pool once. An attack and the minute's round at the same moment both count, one after the other.

  7. A restart of the bot in the middle of a round: the round counts entirely or not at all, and the next minute's round counts once.
  8. A Crown who is still in the server keeps the reign even if the bot briefly thinks otherwise: only a Crown Discord confirms as gone loses it.
  9. If the tipbot is unreachable, the reign still ends and the pool is paid; no RUNES are tipped or promised. When the realm's RUNES wallet holds 1 RUNES or less, or its RUNES prizes aren't connected yet (every server but the Runebase server, until after the update), the reign ends the same way, the pool and the experience paid, and the end result says why no RUNES were paid.

docs.title: A Crown who leaves the server
docs.text: A Crown who leaves the server loses the reign without any reward: until the next round, attacks on them are refused (nothing is spent); then the round ends the reign, the next Crown is drawn from the attackers still in the server (with none of them still here, among the server's players, as above), and the pool stays for the next reign.

docs.title: The pool
docs.text: The pool grows with 5% of every store purchase in the realm and the unclaimed shares of expired credit piles. It shrinks by Robin Hood and Black Hood steals and the tax piles (a tax pile takes its credits from the pool only when it appears: one that can't be posted, or a restart before it appears, leaves them in the pool). The old Crown gets what's left when the reign ends.

docs.title: 🪜 The weekly ladder
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Every ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC to Sunday 23:59:59 UTC) has its own Crown of Chaos ladder. It scores what you did that week (the total is rounded down):

Each … this week Scores Crowns Taken 50 Points Earned 1 Resurgences 20 Bleeds Purged 5 Defuses 5 Mana Drains 2 Silences 10 Bubbles 15 Attacks 1 per 4 Defends 1 per 4 Final Blows 50

A Silence counts only when it lands: one that misses or is dodged scores nothing. Crowns Taken count a Crown won in the draw among the reign's attackers (a Crown drawn among the server's players, a server's first one too, counts none). Points Earned are the points you earn as the Crown; the Crown's skills count when used (Resurgences, Bubbles), per bleed purged or seed defused, and per hit its Mana Drain drained.

  • CoC Weekly Ladder Board on the Crown of Chaos menu (or CoC Weekly Ladder under the channel's posts, answered only to you) shows this week's ladder, ten players a page (Next, Previous), and earlier weeks (Previous Week, Next Week).
  • On Monday (UTC), last week's top 3 get the CoC Winners role; a top-3 player who already has it keeps it ("Role Extended"), and a former winner who isn't in the top 3 loses it. Only a score above 0 counts: after a week nobody scored in, nobody holds the role. If the bot was down on Monday at 00:00, it happens when it starts again.
  • A tie goes to whoever reached the score first; players who left the server are left out.
  • When the staff turn the weekly payouts on (on the Runebase server), last week's positive scores share 1% of the realm's RUNES wallet by rank, once:
Rank Shares of the pool, each 1 10 2 8 3 6 4 5 5 4 6 to 10 3 11 to 20 2 21 to 50 1 51 to 100 0.5

With an empty pool, or one too small for a share each, nobody gets anything and the mana is spent. On a final blow the shares leave the pool first and the old Crown is paid the rest.

docs.title: Silence
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

  • Tree: Offensive skills (for attackers: they work when you attack the Crown)
  • Kind: an attack skill: you pick it for an attack (mana and attack skills)
  • Learn it from: your rank 24
  • Needs first: no other skill
  • Opens: no other skill

In the game: Silences the crown, preventing it from activating Blood Purge, Defuse, Resurgence, and Mana Drain for a duration.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
On a hit, the Crown can't use Resurgence, Blood Purge, Defuse or Mana Drain for the silence's duration (Bubble still works): 415 s for 500 mana at rank 20. A Silence that misses or is dodged scores nothing on the weekly ladder, but its mana is spent.

Every attack costs one Chaos Relic and faces the Crown's rune (runes and damage).

docs.title: Checked in play
docs.text:
• Rank 1 silences the Crown for 35 s, for 25 mana; rank 20 for 415 s, for 500 mana: Resurgence, Blood Purge, Defuse and Mana Drain are off for exactly that long, the Bubble stays. A miss spends the mana and silences nothing; only a Silence that lands scores 10 on the weekly ladder.
  • Silenced, the Crown's four skills are refused even from an old button and stay ready; a Resurgence or a Mana Drain already running goes on.
  • A dodged Silence spends its mana and silences nothing.

docs.title: 👹 Hack & Slash
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

The bot's role-playing game: pick a 🎭 class, fight ⚔️ quick battles against monsters, bring down the 🗿 Jotnar giants together with the server, and duel other players in the 🥊 Arena. You learn 💥 skills, collect 👕 gear, craft items and trade them at the 🔨 auction house.

Where: /hackslash opens the Hack & Slash menu (quick battles, stats, skills, the Arena), /equipment your gear and inventory, /craft crafting.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text: Page What you'll find 🎭 Classes the seven classes, what a new character gets, a page per class 💥 Skills skill points, resets, how each kind of skill works in battle, a page per skill 📈 Attributes and combat attribute points, hitting and missing, damage, armor, resistances, blocking ⚔️ Quick battles zones, monster levels, difficulty, stamina, what a won battle pays 👕 Gear, items and crafting condition, wear and repairs, equipment, inventory, crafting, inscriptions 🔨 The auction house listing fees, bids, buyouts, claims 🗿 The Jotnar the world boss the whole server fights 🥊 The Arena duels against other players

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Dexterity and attack-rating gear make you hit more often; a pure strength build misses more.
  • Pick monsters near your level: those more than 5 levels below you give no experience.
  • Use your free resets after the release to rebuild your characters for the new hit chance.
  • Keep an Anchovy with Anchovy Powder for when a battle goes wrong.

docs.title: 🥊 The Arena
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

/hackslash → Arena → Challenge Opponent: pick a player and challenge them; they join from the public Join Duel message (or from their own Arena menu, Join Duel#…), or turn it down with Decline. You take turns until one of you falls; the survivor wins.

docs.title: Challenging
docs.text:
• You can pick another player as often as you like before pressing Challenge. You can't challenge yourself, a bot, someone who isn't in the server, or a player without a Hack & Slash class: the picker tells you why, on itself. Every refusal (a full duel list too) shows on your Arena screen: a duel you already have open with that player shows that duel, saying so.
  • A challenge waits 5 minutes for the opponent (your screen says when it cancels; opening the challenge again doesn't move that time). Then it's cancelled, and Join Duel says the duel is gone.
  • Decline: the challenged player can turn a challenge down from its message: the message says so, and the challenger's screen too. Only the challenged player can decline (anyone else is told so, privately); once they've joined, the button is gone.
  • Cancel Duel calls off your challenge while nobody has joined. Once your opponent has joined, the duel is on: a Cancel that comes after the join changes nothing, and you're told so.
  • You can have at most 5 open duels, and a player who has 5 can't be challenged, even by several players at the same moment.
  • One duel at a time with the same player: while a challenge or a duel between you two is open, a new challenge either way is refused and you're shown the open one (a double click on Challenge sends one challenge). If they've challenged you, you're told to join or decline theirs.
  • Someone else pressing Join Duel on your challenge only watches, privately: your duel and the message stay as they are.

docs.title: A duel
docs.text:
• The first move is a coin toss. On your turn your screen shows your two attacks (your main and secondary skill, which you can change from the menus below them, at the mana their buttons show), Heal and a Select Target menu; on your opponent's turn it shows whose turn it is.
  • One click, one move: each move button belongs to the turn it was drawn for. A second click of a double click, or a button from an earlier turn, plays nothing and you're told so, privately.
  • A skill picked on a duel screen drawn before you reset your skills changes nothing: the duel screen comes back with your skills as they are now and says why.
  • Heal (3 a duel): your whole move, back to full health and mana; it costs nothing else. The rest of the move goes on as usual: your minions still attack, and effects on both of you count down. You can't heal while stunned or frozen (the button is off). A double click heals once.
  • Targets: your opponent's minions (a Necromancer's Clay Golem, for one) appear in your target menu; pick one and your attacks go there. A minion that falls leaves the duel: it attacks no more and your target goes back to the player.
  • Each turn has 2 minutes; the screen counts them down. If you don't move in time, you lose the duel and your opponent wins: both duel screens and the duel's message in the channel say so. A move made before the time runs out counts; a click after it doesn't. Leaving the server doesn't end a duel: if it's your move, the 2 minutes do.
  • The end: the player still standing wins; if both fall in the same move (a Paladin's Sacrifice, for one), it's a tie. Both screens and the duel's message show the result, and the duel leaves both Arena menus.
  • If the bot restarts during a duel, the time it was down never counts against you: the player whose turn it is gets a DM and 15 minutes before their 2 minutes start (your duel screen from before still works, or open the duel again with /hackslash → Arena → Join Duel#…). A duel the bot lost track of during a very long outage (more than a day) is called off: nobody wins or loses. A challenge still cancels at its time, or as soon as the bot is back if that time passed while it was down.
  • A duel pays nothing: no experience, no credits, no rating. There are no wagers.

docs.title: Skills and gear in a duel
docs.text:
• A buff you cast on your minions too (the Warrior's Battle Orders) lasts its rounds on them, as on you.
  • Auras, buffs and debuffs count once a move: a Paladin's Might hits as hard on the fifth move as on the first. An aura that lowers enemy resistances ( Conviction) lowers only your opponent's, on your move and theirs, and only their magical resistances (fire, cold, lightning, poison and magic), like the Lower Resist curse. A curse such as Amplify Damage counts on every move while it lasts.
  • Resistances stop at 70 % in a duel too, after your gear, auras and curses: a fire or magic hit on a player at 70 % does 30 % of its damage. A curse or Conviction lowers the whole total first, so resistance above 70 on your gear still helps against them.
  • Your gear does in a duel what it does against monsters (item bonuses). Conversion, the skill's or your gear's, never converts your opponent, as in Diablo II: the hit deals its damage and they fight on; it can convert one of their minions (a golem, a summon, a revived monster), which then fights for you with all its skills (it attacks its old master; a monster's Battle Cry or Frozen Armor now for your side, its Bone Armor on itself). The same buff, debuff or curse twice never stacks: the stronger stays and either cast refreshes its rounds, as in ⚔️ quick battles. Gear's chance to make a hit bleed works on your opponent and their minions too: a physical hit that lands may make them bleed like the Warrior's Wound at rank 1.
  • An exploding attack ( Exploding Arrow, for one) hits the player you aim at and its explosion the minion beside them. Corpse Explosion blows up the duel's corpse (a duel with a Necromancer has one from the start) as fire on your opponent and their minions, through their fire resistance.
  • What hits back (Thorns, gear's reflects, Iron Maiden, Retaliate's kick, Radiant Counter's smite) works as against monsters (⚔️ quick battles): its physical part rolls to hit and can miss or be blocked, its fire or magic part never misses. Retaliate's kick answers only a melee hit. A Paladin's Radiant Counter with Radiant Explosion smites back in a duel, explosion and all.

docs.title: 📈 Attributes and combat
docs.text: Where to play: Discord

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
You get 5 attribute points per level to spend on the stats screen (never more than you've earned).

  • Strength: its whole value as % extra physical (and throw) damage.
  • Dexterity: +5 attack rating a point, multiplied by your level's multiplier (below); dexterity from your gear and its inscriptions counts the same as the points you spend.
  • Vitality: health (× your class's health per vitality) and stamina (+1 a point, Assassin 1.25).
  • Energy: mana (× your class's mana per energy).
  • Each level lowers your fire, cold, lightning, poison and magic resistance by 1.

Reset: a stats reset gives every point back, for 0.5 Grilled Coyote Steak With Lingonberry Sauce per point spent, rounded up.

docs.title: Your main and secondary skill
docs.text: The Stats screen has two menus: your main and your secondary skill, the two attack buttons of a battle (each named after its skill, with its mana cost). Each menu lists your class's usable skills; picking one saves it at once, and each menu leaves out the skill the other one holds. The battle screen has the same two menus.

docs.title: Hitting and missing
docs.text:
Physical attacks can miss. Your hit chance is 200% × your attack rating ÷ (your attack rating + the monster's armor) × your level ÷ (your level + the monster's level), kept between 5% and 95%. A level-1 Warrior (attack rating 91) hits a level-1 Flamecaster (armor 55) 62.3% of the time.

  • Your attack rating grows with your level: your class's 50 plus 5 per dexterity point (spent or from gear), times your level's multiplier; attack rating from gear is added on top.
  • Skills and buffs with attack rating % raise it ( Strategic Shout's +40% takes that 62.3% to 69.8%).
  • Monsters block your physical attacks as often as their screen shows (a Zombie 10%).
  • Spells never miss: only physical attacks roll to hit. Magic, Fire, Cold, Lightning and Poison attacks always land, yours and the monsters'.
  • A single-target attack can only miss its own target. Monsters miss you too.
Level 1 5 10 20 25 26 30 40 50 75 100 × attack rating 1.82 3.1 4.7 7.9 9.5 20.22 23.1 30.3 37.5 73.5 121.5

docs.title: Damage
docs.text:
• Critical hits deal 75% more damage.
  • Armor takes armor ÷ (armor + damage) × 95% off physical damage, at most 85%: even a weak hit on heavy armor keeps 15% of its damage.
  • Resistances (fire, cold, lightning, poison, magic) lower the damage of their kind by their %. They stop at 70%, counted after everything that changes them: gear, passive skills, and buffs such as Fade (which raises all five, as its screen says, not physical damage). At 70% a fire hit still deals 30% of its damage; it never heals you.
  • Curses on you (in the Arena, a Necromancer's Lower Resist) lower your whole total before the 70% limit, so resistance above 70% on your gear still protects you from them. Nothing stops a curse from taking a resistance below 0. In the Arena the 70% limit counts after each move's buffs and curses too.
  • Blocking with a shield: your chance is the shield's block × (your dexterity − 15) ÷ (2 × your level), at most 50%. It blocks monsters' physical attacks.

docs.title: 🔨 The auction house
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

List an item from your inventory: the listing fee shown on the duration menu is what you pay. It's the duration's fee (table) × the item's tier (Normal 1, Exceptional 2, Elite 3) × its quality: a Magic Exceptional item costs 2.5 times the fee. Every kind of item can be listed, leg armor included, and is found under its type in the auction house's menu (the class items under "Class-Specific").

You can have at most 5 auctions running or waiting under Claim Auctions. An auction keeps its place until it's sold (bought out, or ended with a bid), or until you take back an item that didn't sell or that you cancelled: take those back (Claim Auctions, or pick them in My Active Auctions) to list more. The inventory's Auction button shows how many places you use (2/5) and is off at 5/5; a sixth listing is refused, on the web too.

  • Prices are typed as plain numbers, rounded down to 8 decimals, from 0.00000001 up to 184,467,440,737.09551615 credits; the starting bid can't be above the buyout, and without a starting bid the buyout is the starting bid.
  • A bid takes your credits; when someone outbids you, you get them back in full. Raising your own bid takes only the difference, and the confirmation says so. A bid at or above the buyout buys the auction at the buyout price ("buy auction #… for …").
  • A buyout pays the seller and refunds the last bidder; the winner claims the item from Claim Auctions.
  • The seller can cancel, even with a bid on it: the bidder gets the bid back and the seller takes the item back from Claim Auctions.
  • When an auction runs out, the seller is paid the highest bid and the channel says who won; with no bids, nobody is paid and the item waits for the seller in Claim Auctions. This happens once, even if the bot was restarting at that moment.
  • Refusals show on your auction house screen: a bid below the starting or current bid, more than you have, on your own auction, on an auction that ended or changed after your confirmation was shown (outbid, bought out, cancelled); a price in another form (0x10, 1e3, +5, 1,5) or out of range; a sixth listing; a claim already made on another screen, without a Hack & Slash character, or with a full inventory. The screen says why (the auction again, or the auction house once the auction is over or gone), and nothing moves.
  • What the screens show is what's stored: 8 auctions a page, the soonest to end first, each with its starting bid, buyout, current bid and bidder and its end; an auction's history, newest first; My Active Auctions (your running auctions, then those waiting to be taken back, marked "Unsold: waiting to be taken back" or "Cancelled: waiting to be taken back") and Claim Auctions (what you can take).
  • Its own house: the Hack & Slash auction house is separate from Runebase World's (the MMORPG's): its listings, bids, items and the 5-listing limit never mix with the other's.

docs.title: 👕 Gear, items and crafting
docs.text: Where to play: Discord

docs.title: Condition, repairs and gear
docs.text:
• Condition: at 00:00 UTC the class you have selected refills its health, mana and stamina; your other classes keep what they had. Pheasant with Blackberry Balsamic Glaze fills your stamina to its maximum.
  • Wear: every round there's a 5% chance one of your equipped items loses 1 durability, and 1.5% with every monster attack, whether it hits you or not (leggings too).
  • Repairs: 1 credit per missing durability point on a Normal item, 2 on an Exceptional one, 3 on an Elite one (a Circlet 1.11). The cost shown, item by item or all at once, is exactly what you pay; durability goes back to the maximum. Without the credits, nothing changes.
  • Equipment: equipping puts the item in its slot and the replaced one back in your inventory (a two-handed weapon also takes off the shield). Gear you're not strong, nimble or experienced enough for stays in your inventory; the strength and dexterity from your other gear and its active inscriptions count toward a requirement (not the item's own). Gear you wear but no longer meet the requirements of (after an attribute reset, taking off a +strength item, or losing levels) gives nothing and shows red on the equipment screen until you meet them again: after a reset, spend your points again. Every bonus an item shows counts while you wear it (item bonuses).
  • Inventory: destroy an item, disassemble it into one crafting material of its quality and tier, or keep it in your stash. The inventory's and the stash's item menus jump straight to the item you pick.
  • Dropping an item: Drop asks first, privately or publicly. A public drop is posted in the channel with a Loot button: the first other player who clicks it gets the item in their inventory (the post then says who), and anyone after them is told it's gone.
  • Stash upgrades: each stash level holds one more item. Upgrade Stash (on the stash screen) shows the next level's cost in Wood Scrap, Nails and Rope, and Preview Stash shows any level's cost and size, level by level or by typing a level ("..."); the upgrade takes exactly the cost shown.
  • Item Info (Equipment → Item Info): the catalog of every item base (with its picture), every magic and rare modifier and every inscription, written as an item's own screen writes it ("Strength Requirement: 25", "Armor: 3 - 5", "+10-20% Enhanced Defense"), with the range each number rolls in, and where it can appear ("Appears on"), its drop level, tier, crafting scrap and repair cost. Page with Previous and Next, or jump ("...") to a page number or a name.
  • The 🏗️ buildings Training Grounds, Arcane Library, Healing Spring, Mana Well, Fitness Foundry and Traveler's Camp make your characters stronger; the Arcane Reliquary makes Magic and Rare drops likelier.

docs.title: Crafting
docs.text:
/craft (or Equipment → Craft):

  • Craft Items: pick the type, family, item and quality: an item costs 3 crafting materials and 1 scrap, goes into your inventory and pays 1 experience. Without the materials, the button is off.
  • Convert Crafting Materials: 3 of a material make 1 of the next tier, for a small credit fee (3 Standard Essence → 1 Elemental Core for 0.3 credits).
  • Inscriptions: a Magic inscription costs 1 Engraving Tool, a Rare one 3. It's drawn from the inscriptions your item's type and your level can get, each stat rolled in its range, and added inactive; activate it to make it the item's inscription (one at a time). Pick an inscription in the item's inscription menu to activate or Remove it; removing asks first ("No, go back!" keeps it) and leaves the item's other inscriptions as they are. Its bonuses then count like the item's own, its armor even on a ring or an amulet, its block on a shield.

docs.title: Item bonuses
docs.text: What an item's screen says is what it does: each number below was checked in play, made from the game's own data, worn, and in a battle round. The item's screen shows the number it rolled; your stats screen moves by exactly that number while you wear it, and back when you take it off. A broken item (durability 0) gives nothing until it's repaired.
