docs.title: 🗿 The Jotnar: a world boss
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

A giant appears in the Hack & Slash channel once every 3 hours. Press Attack Giant to fight it from your own battle screen; each attack costs 5 stamina. It's built for the whole server: its base health is 85,000, and it escapes after 30 minutes.

  • Bigger servers meet bigger giants: up to 100 members a giant has its base health, with 1,000 members half again as much, with 10,000 twice as much; each giant also varies from 80% to 120% of that.
  • You hit it as if it were your own level: its level doesn't make you miss more.
  • When it falls, its 500 credits are split by damage among the fighters still in the server: each gets exactly their share of their damage times the pool, rounded down. Experience is 50 plus 2 for every 1% of the damage you dealt, up to 150 (a giant beaten alone pays 500 credits and 150 experience).
  • When it escapes, it pays only if the server took at least 5% of its health together. Then its fighters share half the pool, by damage, scaled to 25% plus 0.75% for every 1% of its health taken: a giant that escapes with 40% of its health gone pays 55% of 250 credits. Experience is 60% (30 plus 1.2 per 1% of the damage you dealt) at the same scale, loot chances are 70%, and the top three get bonus loot only if they dealt at least 25% of the damage. Hit hard together: bringing it down pays far more.
  • Each giant pays once. Items it drops go to the first player who picks them up.

docs.title: When it comes and goes
docs.text:
• Each 3-hour window (from midnight UTC: 00:00, 03:00, …, 21:00) brings one giant at a random moment, announced with the Jotnar role in the Hack & Slash channel, and with a Join the Battle! link in the server's announcements. Turn the role on or off in /hackslash → Jotnar → Enable Notifications / Disable Notifications.
  • Two giants can be up at once when one comes late in its window and the next early in the next one: the Jotnar menu lists them all, and you can fight either.
  • A restart of the bot changes nothing: a giant still standing keeps the time it had left, and one whose time ran out meanwhile escapes (and pays) as soon as the bot is back.

docs.title: Fighting it
docs.text:
• Two ways in: Attack Giant on its message opens your battle privately; /hackslash → Jotnar → Join Battle turns your Hack & Slash screen into your battle. Only you can use the buttons on your battle; anyone else is told they aren't theirs.
  • Each attack costs 5 stamina, hit or miss. The giant loses exactly the damage your screen shows, and all of it counts as yours. The blow that brings it down counts only the health it had left.
  • Your skills: pick your main and secondary skills on the battle screen; the attack buttons use them at their mana. Without the mana, the button attacks without the skill and spends none.
  • The giant hits back at whoever attacked it, no one else, with its attacks at their odds (Thrymr: Frost Slam 40%, Glacial Breath and Icy Gale 30% each), as hard as your level makes them (a level-30 fighter takes 30% of their full damage, at least 10%), plus its aura every round. Below 80%, 50% and 25% of its health it summons a minion (at most two at a time), which hits every fighter after that, as hard as each fighter's level makes it, every round.
  • Its minions: while one is up, your battle has a Target menu: the giant or a minion, numbered in the order they came (Ice Elemental #1), with their health. Your attacks hit the one you pick. Damage to a minion doesn't count toward your share (only the giant's health does), but a minion brought down stops hitting everyone. When a minion falls it leaves the menu and your target is the giant again; an attack or a pick aimed at a minion that has already fallen is refused on your battle screen (which shows the giant again, saying so), and costs nothing.
  • Falling in battle costs only that attack's stamina: heal, and your damage is still yours. You can't attack while fallen.
  • Heal spends one Anchovy with Anchovy Powder for full health and mana; Stamina spends one Pheasant with Blackberry Balsamic Glaze for full stamina. Both ask first (Accept or Back), and spend nothing when there's nothing to restore, so a double click never costs two. Without one, Accept is off and the screen shows where to get one.
  • Animation turns the battle picture off and on (the same switch as quick battles); Cancel closes your battle.
  • The giant's message shows its health, the last hit and how many are fighting; Leaderboard shows you every fighter's damage and share (the top 10 by name); a fighter who has left the server shows without a share.

docs.title: The end
docs.text:
• Brought down: its message shows the top fighters with their damage and share, and a reward summary lists what each fighter got. Every fighter's loot grows with their share (more kinds of loot from 1%, 2%, 3% and 5% of the damage), the top three get bonus loot, and each giant type has loot of its own.
  • Dropped items: a button each; the first to press it gets the item, and the button then shows who did. You need a Hack & Slash character to pick one up.
  • Escaped: its message says how much of its health the server took and that partial rewards went out, or, below 5%, that it paid nothing.
  • Nothing is lost: a giant brought down just before a restart of the bot pays its fighters as soon as the bot is back, once.
  • Leaving the server before the giant is paid means no share: the fighters still in the server split the pool between them.

Checked in play: fighting from both entrances, the giant's attacks at their odds, its minions and the Target menu, the hit chance at your own level, falling and healing, every refusal, someone else's buttons, double clicks on Accept, twelve fighters attacking at the same moment (no damage lost or counted twice, each paid once), the payouts against the reward rules (a fighter who left: nothing), the dropped items, the leaderboard, the end messages, and a restart before the payout.

docs.title: ⚔️ Quick battles
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

/hackslash → Quick Battle: pick the zone (Shadowed Caverns, Twilight Forest, Frozen Tundra), the monster level and the difficulty, then Start QuickBattle.

  • Monster level: 1 to 100, 25 levels a page; the menu opens on your own level. Levels more than 5 below yours say (No Experience): those monsters pay no experience.
  • Difficulty: ×1 to ×6.75, in steps of 0.25. It multiplies the monsters' health, armor, damage and attack rating, adds the multiplier minus 1 (rounded) to their block, and makes items a little likelier (below).
  • The monsters: a battle has 2 to 5 of them, of the zone and level you picked. Each is the zone's usual monster unless it rolls one of the others, at the chances the setup screen shows. The rare ones (Werewolf, Werebear, Yeti) come 2% of the time each and are worth 5 experience.
  • A quick battle costs 20 stamina (less with the Wizard's Teleport). Pressed twice with stamina for one battle, it starts one battle and takes the stamina once.
  • Out of stamina: Restore Stamina now spends one Pheasant with Blackberry Balsamic Glaze and fills your stamina to its maximum.
  • Each click of a skill button is one round: you attack, then the monsters attack you (a stunned monster skips its attack). A double click plays one round: the second click, or a click on an older battle screen, gets a private "That round was already played" and plays nothing.
  • Dying: a dead character can't start a new battle (nothing is charged). Heal with one Anchovy with Anchovy Powder (health and mana back to full), then Return to QuickBattle (5 stamina) to finish the same battle.
  • Before a battle, or on the results screen for the next one, you can pick Elk with Huckleberry Sauce (double damage) and Baked Cod with Old Bay Butter (+25% experience); each is spent once. With the first, the battle screen says +100% Damage Bonus and your hits deal double damage before the monster's armor.

During a battle:

  • Your condition carries over. Health and mana you lose in a battle stay lost when you win it (the results show them) and when the next one starts; the battle takes 20 stamina. The day's refill fills them again, stamina too, also past 1000.
  • Gear wears a point at a time (5% a round, 1.5% a monster attack, a random item with durability); every point counts on the results' Total Durability Lost, and an item stops at 0 (broken: it gives nothing until repaired).
  • Heal on the battle screen asks first: Decline spends nothing; Accept spends one Anchovy with Anchovy Powder for full health and mana, and you're back in the same battle, the monsters as they were. Without one, Accept is greyed out. Accept clicked twice spends one; so does Restore Stamina (one Pheasant with Blackberry Balsamic Glaze).
  • Back to Town leaves the battle open: the Quick Battle screen then offers Return to QuickBattle #… (Cost: 5 Stamina), the monsters as you left them, your poison and minions still with you. If you start a new battle instead, what's on you (poison, minions, buffs) comes along; winning a battle ends all of it.
  • A restart of the bot doesn't touch an open battle: your battle screen's buttons play on where you were.
  • A battle screen from before a change plays nothing and says why on that screen: a skill picked after you reset your skills (it isn't yours any more; the menus show the skills you have now), Attack after you picked another class (the battle belongs to that other character: Back to Town), or after your character died elsewhere (the death screen, with its heal). Return to QuickBattle without the 5 stamina says you're out of stamina, and takes none.
  • The animation can be switched off (and on) with its button on the battle screen; the round's log then shows what happened.

The monsters' attacks, as the setup screen lists them (the title shows the difficulty you picked, e.g. ×2):

  • Each monster has a default attack and special ones; a special one is used at the chance the screen shows, the default otherwise. Each deals the damage range shown, less your resistance to its damage type (at most 70%, after every buff, aura and curse) and, for physical damage, less what your armor takes.
  • AOE attacks (the Bear's Claw, the Ice Elemental's Frost Nova) hit you and every minion you have out.
  • Battle Cry (Werebear, Yeti) gives every monster its % more physical damage, from the monsters after it in that round, for the rounds shown. Bone Armor (Frost Wraith) puts a damage shield on every monster that takes the first part of your hits. Frozen Armor (Frost Troll) gives every monster its Armor Bonus % (+100%, the same at every difficulty) more armor for its rounds: your hits land less often and lose more to the armor. BloodFang (Werewolf) heals it by its life steal % of the damage it deals.
  • Poison (Snake) puts a poison on you (or on the minion it hits) that ticks every round for the rounds shown, starting that round. Two never stack: a second Poison renews its rounds, and the stronger of the two stays (a level-1 Snake's never replaces a level-10 one's). It stays until its rounds run out or you win the battle.
  • Elemental attacks never miss: Fire Bolt, Venom Strike, Ice Blast, Ice Bolt and Poison always land (the setup screen shows no attack rating for them). Physical attacks (and Stormclaw's Thunderstrike) roll to hit, and your block, dodge and avoid count.
  • Each monster blocks your physical attacks at the Block % the setup screen shows, and takes less physical damage by its Physical Resistance (Bear, Wolf, Werewolf, Werebear, Yeti and the tundra monsters; now on the screen too).
  • Monsters' own reflect never hurts you.

Minions (summons, raised skeletons, a monster your Paladin's Conversion turns):

  • A minion stands on the battle screen with its rounds left and fights from the round you summon it ( Decoy and Oak Sage only stand). Monsters attack a minion 40% of the time it's out (never a trap or a Raven), and how often they hit it depends on the minion's own armor (a fresh skeleton is hit nearly always, a Clay Golem rarely); at 0 health it's gone. Its kills count, and its last kill wins the battle.
  • Every summon keeps to its maximum: summoning more of the same replaces the oldest. Raise Skeleton at rank 1 keeps 1 skeleton, at rank 20 up to 6. A corpse is raised (or exploded) once: the monster then shows Raised, and a skill that needs a corpse turns into your regular attack when none is left.
  • A converted (or revived) monster fights for you with the health it had left and keeps all its skills, now for your side: its Battle Cry gives you and every minion of yours its % more physical damage, its Frozen Armor its % more armor (from the next round, for 5 rounds), its Bone Armor shields itself. Also in the 🥊 Arena.

The same buff twice never stacks (as in Diablo II): when a buff is cast on someone who already has it (your own Battle Cry and a converted Werebear's, two Werebears' on the monsters), the stronger of the two stays in effect, and either cast refreshes its rounds: the buff lasts the longer of what it had left and the new cast's. A weaker cast never lowers a stronger one; the battle screen lists the buff once. Stronger means the larger value (the larger damage %, armor %, shield left, …; on a tie, the one with more rounds left). A converted monster's buff for your side reaches you and the minions you have out at the cast. A different buff of the same kind ( Shiver Armor after Frozen Armor, Werebear after Werewolf) replaces the first. Debuffs and curses follow the same rule (decided 2026-10-29): the same poison, burn, bleed or curse twice never stacks, the stronger stays (the larger damage a round, the larger %) and either refreshes its rounds; your Amplify Damage cast again at a lower rank doesn't lower the one on the monsters. A monster carries one curse at a time: another curse replaces it. A stun or a freeze keeps the longer of the two. The same in the 🥊 Arena.

Explosions: an exploding attack ( Fire Ball, Double Swing, …) hits its target with the attack and the explosion and the monsters right next to it with the explosion; a dead monster in between stops it. Corpse Explosion hits the corpse's neighbours with its % of the corpse's maximum health as fire (less their fire resistance); a monster it kills is the next corpse.

Hitting back: Thorns returns its % of a melee physical hit (not ranged ones, not lightning or fire) through the attacker's armor; gear's Reflect Physical returns ranged hits too, and Reflect Fire a Fire Bolt; a monster under Iron Maiden takes its physical hits back, ranged too. Retaliate kicks back a melee hit that landed (with your boots' damage), Radiant Counter smites back any hit that landed; the battle log says when one of them kills. What comes back by its damage type: a physical part (a reflection, a kick, the shield's smite) rolls to hit with your attack rating, can miss or be blocked, and meets the armor; a fire or magic part (Reflect Fire, Radiant Reflection's magic) never misses. The same in the 🥊 Arena.

A won battle pays once:

  • Experience: 2 per monster, 5 for a rare one, +25% with Baked Cod. A monster more than 5 levels below you gives nothing.
  • The quick battle leaderboards count the win.
  • A roll on the battle prize table (credits go to your wallet).
  • Items the monsters drop: each monster rolls once for an item, at the quality chances its setup screen shows (table below); loot each one once into your inventory. The Arcane Reliquary raises the Magic and Rare chances.
  • Dying pays nothing; a battle left unfinished pays nothing, and starting another doesn't pay for it. Clicking the last attack twice, showing the results again or reopening an old battle pays nothing more.
  • If the bot restarts right after your winning blow, before the results show, the battle is paid when the bot is back (its experience and loot, once). Its dropped items stay with the battle, as if you'd left the results without looting them.

docs.title: 🎭 Classes
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

There are 7 classes. Each class is its own character, with its own attributes, skills, gear, inventory and condition; switching class and back keeps everything. Your level is your rank in the realm, the same for every class.

A new character gets its class's attributes and its full health, mana and stamina (what the class screen shows), and its class's weapon: a Short Sword for the Warrior and the Paladin, a Javelin for the Hunter, a Short Staff for the Wizard, a Katar for the Assassin, a Wand for the Necromancer and a Club for the Druid. All but the Wizard and the Necromancer also get a Buckler.

docs.title: Assassin
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

In the game: Deep within the realms of ancient lore, whispers of a deadly class known as the Nightblade abound. As a Nightblade, you are the very essence of darkness, seamlessly merging with the shadows of the night. Through relentless training and unwavering dedication, you unlock the true potential of rune-forged weaponry and forbidden enchantments. With each level reached, you master new lethal techniques, including blades infused with insidious poisons, illusions that befuddle even the keenest senses, and an innate ability to seamlessly glide through the inky blackness.

A new Assassin starts with these attributes and its full health, mana and stamina (what the class screen shows); 🎭 every class side by side.

Every skill at rank 1 and rank 20: Assassin skills.

docs.title: Druid
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

In the game: The Druid is a master of nature's raw power, seamlessly blending the forces of plant and animal life with potent spellcasting abilities. This versatile class possesses a deep connection with the natural world, granting them the ability to harness elemental energies and transform into ferocious beasts. docs.title: 💥 Skills
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Each class has three skill trees.

  • Skill points: one per level, and the default Throw skill holds one, so a level-3 character has 2 to spend. You can't spend more than you have, and a skill takes at most 20 points.
  • A skill needs its level and the skills listed before it (each skill's page says which).
  • Reset: 5 Grilled Sardines with Sumac Yogurt Sauce in total, whatever the points; it leaves only the base skills.
  • Using skills: on the battle screen you pick a main and a secondary skill; each is a button with its mana cost (" Bonk [💙2]"), charged once when used. A skill you can't use (not enough mana, not in the right shape, or without the weapon it needs, like Magic Arrow without a bow) shows as Attack and makes the regular attack instead, for free.
  • What a skill does at each rank is what its skill screen shows: the battle uses the same numbers.

docs.title: Free resets at the release
docs.text: Every character that existed before this release gets one free attribute reset and one free skill reset: the reset screen says free, nothing is spent, and it's used once (also on a double click). After it, resets cost their steaks and sardines again. New characters don't get them.

docs.title: How skills work in battle
docs.text:
Kind What happens (examples the tests play) attack hits the selected monster ( Bonk adds its flat damage, then its %) area hits every monster ( Cleave) volley several hits, after the first on random living monsters ( Strafe rank 1: 3 arrows) chain "targets N" hits N times, hopping between monsters ( Guided Arrow rank 1: 4 hits) explodes the target takes the hit and the explosion, its neighbours the explosion ( Fire Ball) burn, poison ticks once a round for its rounds ( Inferno "rounds 4" ticks 4 times; Fire Wall burns every monster) buff on you for its rounds ( Battle Cry +35% damage, Battle Orders +40% health, Strategic Shout +40% attack rating, Cloak of Shadows dodge and avoid, War Cry parry) debuff on the monster ( Amplify Damage: +15% physical damage taken; Inner Sight: −40 armor on every monster; Howl: −10% armor). Casting it again replaces it aura works while it's your main or secondary skill ( Might +20% physical damage, Holy Fire burns every monster, Concentration mana steal) heal Paladin Heal: 10% of your maximum health stun a stunned monster skips its attack ( Tornado; a Screech stun lasts the round; Tempest Bind for its rounds) shapeshift Werewolf and Werebear: the Druid skills that need the shape fall back to the regular attack without it summon a minion fights at your side for its rounds ( Clay Golem rank 1: 275 health, 10 rounds; Raise Skeleton needs a corpse) charges every third use releases the charged effect ( Tiger Strike) passive always on (some only with their weapon)

Mirror ( Warrior) copies your attack at its own damage bonus (−50% at rank 1). Paladin Cleansing removes your debuffs and heals 5%.

docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

  • Class: Assassin

In the game: An attack with a chance to freeze the enemy that stores a charge; the third strike deals its cold damage and explodes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• It hits the monster you selected.
  • Every third use releases its charged effect, then it starts over.
  • Its physical damage rolls to hit (your hit chance), and monsters can block it.
  • It costs its mana once, when used. Without enough mana, or without the weapon or shape it needs, its button says Attack and makes the regular attack instead, for free.

docs.title: Cold Arrow
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

  • Class: Hunter
  • Tree: Bow and Crossbow Skills
  • Kind: an attack
  • Learn it from: level 6 (your rank)
  • Needs first: no other skill
  • Opens: Ice Arrow, Guided Arrow
  • Weapon: a bow
  • Mana: 3 at rank 1, 3 at rank 20

In the game: Enchants an arrow: converts half of the arrow's physical damage to cold, adds cold damage and a chance to freeze your enemy.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• It hits the monster you selected.
  • Its cold damage never misses: only physical attacks roll to hit.
  • It costs its mana once, when used. Without enough mana, or without the weapon or shape it needs, its button says Attack and makes the regular attack instead, for free.

docs.title: Checked in play
docs.text: • Half of your arrow's physical damage (with its bonuses) turns to cold: that half passes armor and meets cold resistance, the other half stays physical; plus its own cold (1 at rank 1, 20 at rank 20). A freezing hit freezes the monster for its rounds, the round it lands included: 15% for 2 rounds at rank 1, 72% for 12 rounds at rank 20. 3 mana.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• It hits the monster you selected.

  • It costs its mana once, when used. Without enough mana, or without the weapon or shape it needs, its button says Attack and makes the regular attack instead, for free.

docs.title: Checked in play
docs.text:
• A hit that lands has its chance (1% at rank 1, 4.8% at rank 20) to turn the monster into a minion that fights for you with the health it had left, for its rounds (10, 48); at most 1 at once (3 at rank 20). A monster the hit kills isn't converted. The converted monster keeps all its skills, now for your side: its Battle Cry or Frozen Armor buffs you and your minions, its Bone Armor shields itself. The same buff from two sources never stacks: the stronger stays, either cast refreshes its rounds.
  • In the Arena it never converts your opponent, as in Diablo II: the hit deals its damage and they fight on; it can convert one of their minions.

docs.title: Heists and clans
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

In a heist you steal experience from another player, not credits. Buffs, gear, pets, a building and a clan change the odds. Every heist counts on a monthly ladder; its best players win a role, and the ladder can pay RUNES prizes.

Where: /heist (pick the player and the attack type), or /start → Activities → Heist for the heist menu (joining, buffs, gear, clans, the attack guide). /heistboard shows the ladders, /browseclans lists the clans.

docs.title: Joining and leaving
docs.text:
• Join from the heist menu (Join → Confirm join). You need a minimum amount of experience, which the menu shows ("You need at least … experience to join the heist games!"). Only players who joined can heist and be heisted.
  • If your experience drops below that minimum after a heist, you lose your place in the heist game.
  • Leaving puts you in a protective bubble: nobody can heist you, and you can't heist. The bubble has limits:
Rule Limit Leaving the heist (a bubble), per calendar month 3 Earliest bubble after joining 2 days No bubble in the last days of the month 3 days Waiting time to rejoin after bubble 1 of the month 24 hours Waiting time to rejoin after bubble 2 of the month 48 hours Registering a clan 15,000 credits Members in a clan at most 5 Accepted joins per clan per month at most 10
  • After your 3rd bubble of a month you can't rejoin until the next month begins: the heist menu's join button stays locked, and /rolepanel (the public panel) refuses privately.
  • Joining stays open in the month's last 3 days; only leaving is closed then.
  • Left in an earlier month, or lost your place to low experience? You can rejoin right away once you have enough experience again, also in a new month.
  • /rolepanel (the heist role's Earn or Remove button) does the same: leaving within 2 days of joining, or rejoining before the wait is over, is refused with the time you can: privately under the public role panel, on the heist menu from its join and leave screens.
  • Being heisted is no bubble: you stay in the heist, protected only by the 6 hits a day.
  • A week without an attack and you leave the heist: 7 days after you join, and 7 days after each of your attacks, you're out of the heist if you haven't attacked since (being heisted doesn't count). It isn't a bubble: you can rejoin at once, and from your rejoin you have a new week. The heist channel names the players who left.

docs.title: Energy and hits
docs.text:
• You have 3 heist energy a day, and you can be heisted 6 times a day. Both refill at 00:00 UTC, when the bot's midnight refill runs (a few seconds after midnight it may still count the old day). A heist counts on the ladder of the month it's made in: 23:59:59 on the last day is that month, 00:00:00 on the 1st the new one.
  • An attack costs 1 energy (unless you recover it: one heist). Every heist on you uses one of your 6 daily hits, also a blocked one.
  • Mímisbrunnr (in the heist menu): sacrifice an eye, once a month, to refill your heist energy and your daily hits. It costs nothing else (experience, credits, buffs and your score stay as they are), counts for your clan too, and is told in the heist channel. It's closed in the last 3 days of the month. A second eye the same month, or one from outside the heist, is refused privately; a double click takes one eye.

A heist is refused, and nothing changes, when you're out of energy, when you target yourself, a player in a bubble or who never joined, a player who left the server, a player already hit 6 times today, or a member of your own clan; also when the player bubbles or leaves the server while your heist is starting, and when the heist would pay you more than 15,000 experience at once (with a big backlog of heist quests: see quests). If you haven't joined, /heist tells you heists aren't enabled for you; on a server not set up for heists (no heist role, or no heist channel for the heists' log), it says so. Every refusal is private, also from the heist menu's attack guide. A double click on the guide's Attack button attacks once: the second click is told the attack was already made.

The buttons under every heist log (Heist, the monthly ladders, Legend) work for anyone and answer only the one who clicks.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Every charge that applies to your side is used on every heist: eat buffs for the heists you're about to do.
  • A clan protects you (1 less experience lost) and keeps clanmates from heisting you.
  • Super buffs are limited to 5 a month.

docs.title: ⚡ Clans
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

  • Register a clan from the clan menu: it costs 15,000 credits (the only clan action that costs credits). With fewer credits, a name already taken, or a name under 3 letters, nothing is spent, and the clan menu says why; if something goes wrong while registering, nothing is spent either.
  • Join by request: find a clan with /browseclans (every open clan, page by page) and ask to join; the leader accepts or declines. A full clan can't accept. If you founded your own clan meanwhile, the leader is told you're already in a clan.
  • The leader can pass the leadership and kick members. When the last member leaves, the clan closes.
  • Whatever a clan screen refuses (a taken name, a full clan, a member who already left, a button from before the leadership passed on) is said on that screen, which shows the clan as it is now.
  • A clan accepts at most 10 joins a month: a member who leaves and comes back uses another. Once the 10 are used, the clan takes no new requests that month, and waiting ones can only be declined.
  • Leave a clan and you lose its protection at once: your former clanmates can heist you.
  • Clanmates can't heist each other, and a deflection never lands in the attacker's clan.
  • A heist between members of two clans also counts for both clans' ladders.

docs.title: 🏆 Score, ladders and prizes
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Your heist score is: 5 per energy used + 1.25 × experience gained (rounded) − experience lost + 3 per hit taken. The energy counts even when it was recovered; a blocked hit counts nothing. The ladder counts each heist's full amounts: a defender with less experience than the heist takes still has the full loss on the ladder. The score is worked out from your month's totals, so one heist can add a point less than the one before: three raids of 11 score 19, 19 and 18 (56 in all).

On a tie, the player whose ladder entry changed least recently ranks first; any heist on you changes it, also a blocked one.

  • /heistboard (or /start → Ranks → Heist Board) shows this month's clan ladder first, then the all-time clans, this month's players and the all-time players, 10 to a page: Next and Previous go through every page, each row once, and the monthly ladders have Previous Month and Next Month.
  • Monthly winners: last month's top 5 heisters get the heist winners role, and only they keep it. A player whose month ended at zero or below gets no role.
  • Winning clan: on the 1st, the members of last month's best clan get the clan winners role, and only they keep it; the winners are announced in the heist channel, once a month, in a post titled with the month (such as "Heist Clan Winners of October 2026") that names the clan (the players' ladder post is "New Heist Ladder Month Started"). A clan whose month ended at zero or below wins nothing.
  • Monthly RUNES prizes, when the staff pay them (on the Runebase server): last month's best heisters share 2% of the realm's RUNES wallet by rank (table below); only positive scores are paid. Only the staff pay the clans' prize (it's never paid automatically): the best clans share 1.5% by clan rank, split equally among each clan's members. Players who left the server are left out, and the next player moves up. A month is paid once.

docs.title: 🗡️ Attacks and defence
docs.text: Where to play: Discord

docs.title: One heist
docs.text:
The attacker gains 10 experience and the defender loses 10, plus the attack type you chose:

Attack type Effect ⬆️ +1 Increased Experience Gain you gain 1 more ⬇️ +1 Increased Opponent Experience Loss the defender loses 1 more ⚡ +5% Recovery Chance 5% more chance to keep your energy +3% Gain Retribution Fury 3% chance to earn a Retribution Fury charge +4% Gain Assault Fortification 4% chance to earn an Assault Fortification charge

Then the chances roll:

  • Recovery: the attack costs no energy (it still scores its energy on the ladder).
  • Block: the defender blocks; nobody gains or loses experience, but it's still one of the defender's daily hits.
  • Counter-attack: the defender strikes back: the defender wins back 10 and the attacker loses 10 (so with the default attack type, the attacker ends at +1 and the defender at 0). It counts as a hit on the attacker's ladder, not on their daily hits. It's the defender's attack and the raider's defence for experience: the defender's experience bonuses ( Wild Turkey, Fried Squirrel, Odin's Furyblade, Forseti's Judgment, Phoenix Chick, Thunderbird) add to it, the raider's block and experience protections ( Moose, Mackerel, the Barrier Draught, Assault Fortification, defending gear, Ghost Cat, the block pets, the clan) work against it; it never gives energy back or earns a buff. It wins back at most 14 and takes at most 13, at least 6. The log says what it really moved: a defender with no experience left wins back 0 (nothing was taken), and an attacker with only 3 loses 3.
  • Deflect: the heist lands on another heister instead, who takes the hit; the defender is untouched (and gets a deflect on their stats). It never lands on a member of the attacker's clan; with nobody to take it, there's no deflection.

Nobody's experience goes below 0: a defender with 4 experience loses 4, and the attacker still gains the full amount. What a heist takes doesn't depend on levels: a new heister and one at the top rank take the same from each other. An attacker gains at most 15 in one heist and a defender loses at most 14, and at least 6 (with every protection); a hit both blocked and counter-attacked only costs the attacker 10 and only gives the defender 10.

After each heist the attacker gets a private message ("Heist Energy Left: n/3"), and the heist channel shows everyone what happened: each side's buffs, the experience moved, the scores, energy and hits, and each side's loot and the quests the heist completed for them (every quest in their loot summary; a box of its own for each that fits in the message, however many both sides completed).

docs.text:

An attacking perk works on your own attacks, a defending perk when you're hit. In a counter-attack, an experience perk of the defender (Phoenix Chick, Thunderbird) adds to it, and a block or experience perk of the raider (Ghost Cat, the block pets) protects against it; the others do nothing in it. Every pet's perks: 🐾 Pets.

  • Heist Clan Protection: a defender who is in a clan loses 1 less experience, and so does a raider in a clan who is counter-attacked.

Eat a buff from the heist menu's Heist Buffs (every buff of every game: 🍲 Buffs by game): pick it, then Consume all you hold, or Consume and type how many (a box closed without a number eats nothing). Each one you eat is one charge. The screen's Heist Buffs and Heist Super Buffs buttons explain them, with a way back to the heist menu. Every charge you hold that applies to your side is used on every heist you're in, one charge each, whether it changed the outcome or not.   • A buff used "only when you're counter-attacked" ( Moose, Mackerel, Barrier Draught, Assault Fortification) stays when you attack and nobody strikes back. A defending-only buff ( Seared Tuna, Retribution Brew, Retribution Fury) stays when you attack, and an attacking-only one ( Grilled Eel, Frigg's Elixir) when you defend; Wild Turkey and Fried Squirrel wait for your attack or your counter-attack.
  • A deflected heist uses none of the defender's charges (they weren't hit); the raider's are used once, on the heist that lands, with the new defender's.
  • Super buffs: at most 5 a month. You must be on this month's heist ladder: you are once you joined, attacked or were attacked this month (in the heist since an earlier month, you're refused until then, and nothing is taken). For a clan member, the clan must be on this month's clan ladder too (opening the heist menu puts it there); both count them. A 6th is refused and nothing is taken.
  • Super buff charges you haven't used are gone at the month change: the new month's first run resets them to 0. Your other buffs stay.
  • Earned buffs come from the attack types, and from gear and pets that add a chance to earn them: each win adds one charge.

docs.title: 🛡️ Heist gear
docs.text:
Where to play: Discord

Heist gear is crafted with scrap from the heist gear menu (it costs exactly the scrap listed). You wear one item per slot: shield, weapon, helm, armor and ring. Equipping another item in a slot takes the first one off.

  • Without Tactical Shift (the default), your neutral set counts both when you attack and when you defend.
  • With Tactical Shift (Enable Tactical Shift in the heist menu), your offensive set counts when you attack and your defensive set when you defend; the neutral set rests.
  • An attacking bonus works when you attack, a defending bonus when you defend.
  • A counter-attack is the defender's attack and the raider's defence for experience: Odin's Furyblade and Forseti's Judgment also add to your counter-attack when you defend, and the defending block and experience pieces (Njord's takes 1 off, a block item can block it) protect you when you're counter-attacked as the raider. A counter-attack never gives energy back or earns a buff, so the recovery and earned-buff pieces do nothing in it.
  • With Tactical Shift each side keeps the set it's wearing in a counter-attack: the raider their offensive set (its defending pieces protect them, the defensive set's don't), the defender their defensive set.
  • Every item's numbers are the ones its gear screen, the crafting screen and the heist menu show, and the heist uses exactly those; every slot adds up.

  • 2% more to earn a Retribution Fury charge (3% + 2% with the Gain Retribution Fury attack).

docs.title: How gear works
docs.text:
You craft it with scrap from the heist gear menu (exactly the scrap listed) and wear one item per slot. An attacking bonus works when you attack, a defending bonus when you defend. A counter-attack is the defender's attack and the raider's defence for experience: an attacking experience bonus also adds to your counter-attack when you defend, and a defending block or experience bonus also protects you when you're counter-attacked as the raider; a counter-attack never gives energy back or earns a buff. Without Tactical Shift your neutral set counts both ways; with it, the offensive set attacks and the defensive set defends, and in a counter-attack each side keeps the set it's wearing (the raider their offensive set, the defender their defensive set). Every slot adds up. More: 🛡️ heist gear.

Other items for the armor slot: Baldur's Reflective Shell, Einherjar's Rejuvenating Cuirass.

• Where you get it: bought in the 🏪 store; a prize of fishing (extra prizes), 🏹 hunting (extra prizes), 🧭 expeditions, 🎰 Loot Reels.

  • Store: 2.5 credits in the 🏪 store; sells back for 1.875 credits (75%, more with a Trade Post).

docs.title: 📦 Pet tokens
docs.text: A pet token is spent to find a pet of its rarity (getting a pet); there's one for each of the six rarities.

docs.title: Common Pet Token
docs.text:
• Where you get it: bought in the 🏪 store; a prize in 11 prize tables (below).
  • Pets: consumed to find a pet of its rarity (getting a pet).
  • Store: 5 credits in the 🏪 store; sells back for 3.75 credits (75%, more with a Trade Post).
A prize in 11 prize tables

fishing (extra prizes), 🏹 hunting (extra prizes), 🧭 expeditions, heists, 🎰 Loot Reels, 🔤 WordWeaver, dice, 🗣️ chat points, ⛰️ bumps, 🗳️ votes, 🎨 memes.
